messages.646:
The plant was still growing there, but if yesterday hadn't
taken place, I wouldn't have been able to distinguish it.
messages.767:
Turning my back on the plant, I started heading back to
class.
messages.872: Tsukishiro had been standing behind me.
messages.909:
Her presence wasn't even noticable; how long had she been
standing there?
messages.1032:
Thinking for a while, she eventually took off her gloves,
and patted her doll.
messages.1169: "H, hello... uh, this is Tsukishiro speaking, right?"
messages.1278:
Tsukishiro calmly shook her head no, her twin curled
ponytails swinging side-to-side with her head.
messages.1386: "Therefore, the one speaking must be me, Piros."
messages.1444:
"There's no such thing as a doll, albeit one with a name,
speaking on it's own. It's ventriloquism, no? You're really
skilled."
messages.1567:
Tsukishiro's head turned upwards, staring at me. Her mouth
curled into a frown, her eyes still unwavering.
messages.1732:
"...Alright, alright, I get it. That doll is talking. That's
what's going on."
messages.1835:
Somehow, Tsukishiro... I mean, the doll, insisted that it
was the one talking.
messages.1907:
Strange as it may be (although par for the course), whether
it's the doll talking or Tsukishiro talking doesn't really
matter.
messages.2014:
Considering things that have happened, and are happening
right now, that's not anything to be surprised about.
messages.2082:
At a time like this, all you really need to do is nod and
smile.
messages.2159: "My name's not "doll"! It's Piros. Alice's only friend."
messages.2270: He's a pretty big loudmouth for a doll.
messages.2311:
"Anyway, Tsukishiro. Did you get back your student
notebook?"
messages.2418:
Alice's answer was barely audible, her head nodding slightly
once at the same time.
messages.2465:
She hasn't really had a reason to talk so far, but I get the
feeling that she's probably not very good at it to start
with.
messages.2587:
"She recieved it from Seiba-san as soon as we returned
home."
messages.2659:
The doll in Alice's arms, unchangingly expressionless,
answered for her. Somehow, he seems rather... unsubtle.
messages.2760: "...Being explained to by a doll is still a weird feeling."
messages.2828:
I'm not in their rhythm at all. The relationship between
Tsukishiro and that doll was still a mess of confusion to
me.
messages.2920:
Trying to distract myself, I idly stared at the water can at
my feet.
messages.2959: "Still taking care of that plant today?"
messages.3073:
"It's a very important flower, so of course we'd have to
take care of it extremely well."
messages.3139: Piros elaborated further on Alice's terseness.
messages.3176: "Not saying you shouldn't. But is this really a flower?"
messages.3236:
Even if it wasn't stepped on or whatever, it seems so weak,
that a strong gust of wind could probably blow it into the
air.
messages.3362: Refitting her gloves, Tsukishiro picked up the watering can.
messages.3407:
Repeating yesterday's routine, she calmly strode over to the
plant, and started to water it.
messages.3526:
For a split second, Tsukishiro had turned her head to me and
opened her mouth slightly. But before a word could escape
her lips, her concentration went back to the plant and
watering can.
messages.3649: I called out the doll's name.
messages.3678:
Yet all the doll did was sit in Tsukishiro's arms quietly,
wearing a never-fading smirk.
messages.3818:
It must be ventriloquism. It said so much that it could talk
by itself, yet now, it seemed dead as a doornail.
messages.3925:
Tsukishiro then stood up, having finished watering the
plant.
messages.4035:
With the watering can in one hand and the doll in the other,
she hurried back to the school building.
messages.4187:
I kicked the ground in a mixture of confusion and
frustration, creating a cloud of dust.
messages.4228: "...The hell is up with that girl?"
messages.4298:
But, even as incomprehensible as it is, I can't help but be
intrigued by it.
messages.4362:
Especially of that Piros, whether it's controlled by
ventriloquism or whether he's what he claims he is.
messages.4457: My eyes traveled over to the Tsukishiro's adopted plant.
messages.4498:
The faint rays of the sun were reflecting off the residue
drops of water, making the plant look as if it was shining.
messages.4625:
I thought, as I finally started digging into my lunch of
Hiroshima pastry cakes.
messages.4867:
Thinking about Tsukishiro, I visited the gym rear and met
her again.
messages.4941:
As before, she let the doll do the talking for her. I asked
her a lot of questions, but she remained just as
tight-lipped as yesterday.
messages.5080:
Looking at the flower she was raising, I knew one thing for
sure; she'd keep coming back here.

messages.153: I should eat something different once in a while...
messages.200:
I thought that as I exited the school premises, and found
two familiar faces.
messages.399: "You guys aren't having lunch? What're you doing?"
messages.476:
"Nope, we just thought we should eat something different
once in a while."
messages.540: Suginami expressed my own thoughts clear as day.
messages.581: Are we having a good synchro rate? I'm going to be sick.
messages.693: "Er... I was thinking the same thing."
messages.762:
"Ohhh, indeed, indeed! Our minds are one. Indeed, our
burning friendship binds us together!"
messages.850: I waved my hand dismissively at Suginami.
messages.885:
Whether or not I accepted it though, I really was thinking
that.
messages.960:
"Then, let the three of us experience the most wonderous of
lunchtimes!"
messages.1060: "Uh, you mean eating at a restaurant?"
messages.1133:
"Mm. You said you knew a good Japanese-style restaurant,
Kudou. Elaborate!"
messages.1253:
"If we go outside to eat now, we definitely won't make it
back for afternoon classes."
messages.1354:
As Kudou's serious face lightly admonished Suginami, I
nodded sagely at his side.
messages.1473: And what would Nemu say if she found out.
messages.1512: "Let's just go to a convenience store."
messages.1616: "...Yeah, that kind of change is acceptable."
messages.1712:
Then, the three of us walked to a nearby convenience and
provisions store.
messages.1790:
Just buying things isn't amazingly interesting, but doing it
with friends always makes it more enjoyable.
messages.2075:
Wanting a change from the usual lunchtime menu, I went with
Suginami and Kudou to a nearby convenience store to buy some
take-out.

messages.133:
The class was bubbling with excitement today. Apparently
there was another transfer student in the neighbouring
class.
messages.228:
Apparently, it's a girl, and she has some strange reasons
for transferring here, from what I heard chattering around
my desk.
messages.335:
I can't really believe that this transfer student would
transfer to a different school out of an unrequited love...
messages.463:
With Koyomi-sensei's entrance into the classroom, the bustle
of the classroom died quickly as the attendance was marked.
messages.564:
"This week is examination week, so make sure you study hard
for it."
messages.652:
Koyomi-sensei's "words of encouragement" certainly didn't
sound like them.
messages.704: More like a threat to the students.
messages.725:
Koyomi-sensei went through the usual things, and then ended
homeroom.
messages.962:
Today, a transfer student came into the other class, and
caused some excitement in this one.
messages.1034:
The transfer student's dramatic love... sounds more like a
kid's dream, and the subject was quickly changed to worrying
about the coming exams.

messages.127:
The scratching of chalk on blackboard was closely mirrored
by the scribbling of pen on note paper.
messages.241:
Just as I realized I had miswritten an earlier passage of
text, it was erased from the blackboard.
messages.370:
At the very front of the class, right in front of the
teacher's desk, Nemu had her head down, furiously copying
notes.
messages.460: I can just copy them from Nemu later, I suppose.
messages.664:
I didn't manage to write down a passage from the blackboard
before it was erased. But it's still okay. Nemu's in this
class.
messages.761:
While Nemu's around, there's no need to worry about taking
notes.

messages.178: "And that ends the class. Weekly duty, rise."
messages.254: After calling out attendance, Koyomi bade us farewell.
messages.329: I make a small guts pose under my desk.
messages.370: She ended the class 5 minutes earlier than usual.
messages.458:
I bow with respect and affection for Koyomi-sensei, while my
lower half was tingling... meaning my leg, really.
messages.555:
"(Although at this rate, during lunch period, I'm almost
certainly going to get entangled into Sakura again...)"
messages.629:
--The sight of her face in my mind's eye made me stop in my
tracks.
messages.823: Holding her purse, Nemu walked past my side.
messages.883: "That's odd... did you forget your lunchbox?"
messages.924:
Unlike myself who eats at the cafeteria nearly every day,
Nemu usually brings a lunchbox from home.
messages.1059: "Noo... I just felt like eating at the cafeteria today."
messages.1115: She talked to me with a slightly sulky voice.
messages.1225: "Sigh... because of the girl with puberty problems."
messages.1281: Rolling her eyes a bit, Nemu left the classroom.
messages.1358:
I didn't really understand what Nemu meant, but decided not
to think too much about it.
messages.1491:
As I turn around, Mako's face is the first thing in my
vision.
messages.1630:
"Nothing. Just trying to perfect a scowl to neutralize your
punch."
messages.1744:
"...Still being stupid. Onee-chan is waiting for me, I'm
going now."
messages.1827: With a wave of my hand, I see her back off.
messages.1910:
Opening the door to the corridor, I decided on my lunchtime
spot.
messages.2115:
Class ended 5 minutes earlier than normal. I cheered and did
a small guts pose.

messages.180: I carried some yakisoba bread and croquette bread with me.
messages.234:
The two breads were on a bargain sale, and I had to fight
through several students to grab them. They're a popular
item.
messages.363: "...I bet a cow could graze here for a long time."
messages.410:
I find a good bench with some sun shining onto it, and
approach it.
messages.564: I sat next to her, putting the bag down next to me.
messages.603: Not like there's any other place to sit, besides on her lap.
messages.697:
"That's really a lot, Asakura-kun. You must've spent a lot
on that."
messages.755:
"It'd be worth it. I won't get fat on it or anything
anyway."
messages.826: "Guys have it lucky, they don't have to worry about that."
messages.917:
I probably should've said something helpful then, but I
couldn't think of anything.
messages.1005: "Within 3 years, you'd surely find a cute girlfriend!"
messages.1104:
An exact figure for a cloudy subject... where'd the whole
subject come from anyway?
messages.1284: "Huh? Kotori, what's up with you today?"
messages.1419: She placed her lunchbox on her lap.
messages.1549:
With her acceptance and smile, I take the yakisoba bread out
from my pocket.
messages.1648:
"Well, as long as it tastes good, how it looks shouldn't
matter..."
messages.1751: Chewing the bread from my first bite, I look towards Kotori.
messages.1835: "That's amazing, it's usually impossible to get that."
messages.1876:
"Yup, it was a battle of epic proportions to acquire this
treasure."
messages.2060: It's just a normal yakisoba bread...
messages.2364: I ate lunch with Kotori in the courtyard.
messages.2405:
When I took out my Yakisoba bread, Kotori requested for a
bite.

messages.228:
As proof, I held out the bread to her, and her mouth quickly
opened.
messages.269: "Ah... it does have blue filling though..."
messages.359: "And it'll stain my teeth? Don't worry about that."
messages.430: "I always clean my teeth after meals."
messages.490: That's a girl for you. That area is always clean for them.
messages.607: She took a bite from the bread, chewing carefully.
messages.686: Seeing her smile, a thought popped into my head.
messages.793: Swallowing rather hastily, her cheeks turned a bright red.
messages.855:
"Now that I think about it, this is an indirect kiss isn't
it..."
messages.906:
"Yeah... and when you return the bread, the two-way indirect
kiss will be complete!"
messages.982: I gave her a devillish grin.
messages.1252:
Thanks to my joke about the indirect kiss, Kotori did
something quite unlike her usual self.
messages.1374: "It was an indirect kiss, I had to..."
messages.1550: "A, anyway, please take my lunchbox in return."
messages.1612: She handed me her lunchbox with a sweet smile.
messages.1678: I decided to keep my mouth shut, for once.
messages.1767: "Ohh. In that case, you can have this one too."
messages.1812: I gave her the uneaten croquette bread as well.
messages.2015: "The octupus made out of sausage, I mean."
messages.2101:
The lunchbox showed obvious care in catering to all the
major food groups and giving nourishment to the recipient.
messages.2277:
We started our lunch in peace, in the deserted school
courtyard.
messages.2537:
But once I handed over the bread and she took a bite, the
subject of indirect kisses came up...
messages.2623:
The embarassed Kotori then quickly finished the whole bread
before the possibility could become the truth.
messages.2689: At least I got a good lunchbox out of it.

messages.165: "(But wouldn't this be an indirect kiss...)"
messages.291:
Kotori's eyes became round while staring at the yakisoba
bread, apparently thinking about something.
messages.415: "Ah, but, if I eat from the opposite side..."
messages.662: I held out the bun, and Kotori happily took it.
messages.794: "...Is it okay if I open the bag from the opposite side?"
messages.927: "I can't let it be an indirect kiss..."
messages.974:
Mumbling something, she took a bite from the side opposite
the side I had taken a bite from.
messages.1112: "... But I certainly don't mind receiving an indirect kiss!"
messages.1208: "Come on, if you've had enough, give it back already."
messages.1251: I gave her a devillish grin.
messages.1551: "It was an indirect kiss, I had to..."
messages.1727: "A, anyway, please take my lunchbox in return."
messages.1789: She handed me her lunchbox with a sweet smile.
messages.1855: I decided to keep my mouth shut, for once.
messages.1944: "Ohh. In that case, you can have this one too."
messages.1989: I gave her the uneaten croquette bread as well.
messages.2192: "The octupus made out of sausage, I mean."
messages.2278:
The lunchbox showed obvious care in catering to all the
major food groups and giving nourishment to the recipient.
messages.2454:
We started our lunch in peace, in the deserted school
courtyard.
messages.2714:
But once I handed over the bread ahd she took a bite, the
subject of indirect kisses came up...
messages.2800:
The embarassed Kotori then quickly finished the whole bread
before the possibility could become the truth.
messages.2866: At least I got a good lunchbox out of it.

messages.141: Time to secure today's afternoon rations.
messages.193: If they're available, I'd aim for the yakisoba bread.
messages.230:
But the competition is fierce... it might be sold out by now
already.
messages.294: I guess I'd take a croquette bread if that happens...
messages.335: In any case, better go now.
messages.393: Turning around, I bumped into Tamaki.
messages.491: "You're not wearing your miko dress this afternoon?"
messages.562: "It isn't quite something I wear at all times."
messages.655: I was mostly joking, but her serious reply was somehow cute.
messages.759: "That costume is only for special circumstances..."
messages.866: Tamaki wouldn't say any more than that.
messages.897: Well, if she wants to keep it private, I can't say anything.
messages.940: I don't want to force anything out of her either.
messages.985:
"If you were hanging around here, I guess you had to buy
lunch today?"
messages.1079:
"Yes. As I had forgotten my lunchbox today, I thought that
if I didn't hurry, there would be nothing left."
messages.1267:
Tamaki held in her hands, the prized possession that men
would come to blows for; yakisoba bread.
messages.1378: Praying for a positive response, I enquired.
messages.1413: Tamaki's expression turned to one of ponderance.
messages.1476: "I don't believe so... the one I have, was the last."
messages.1656:
"Well... at the time I left, there was a sudden flood for
bread at the store, so..."
messages.1821: Looks like I'd have to skip lunch today.
messages.1966: Seeing my crestfallen state, Tamaki started to speak.
messages.2015:
"Yeah, there aren't many in stock every day. On top of that,
it's delicious, so there's always a scramble for them."
messages.2109:
Even with the luck of the devil himself, you'd be
hard-pressed to eat it more than once a week.
messages.2211: "And, you like this type of bread?"
messages.2373:
Tamaki's envisage transformed to that of an angel,
descending from the cloudy sky.
messages.2439:
Or if not that, a spider hanging from it's web in the depths
of hell.
messages.2519: But, if I take this, what about Tamaki?
messages.2633: "It's fine. I still have a packet of melon bread, as well."
messages.2701: She showed me her other packet, smiling.
messages.2753: Those actions and movements... how cute.
messages.2874: Today, I am a dog with it's tail up.
messages.2923: People may say things about it being an unfair trade,
messages.2972: But I have no ears for them today.
messages.3019:
The words I heard immediately after, didn't tally too well
with my stance.
messages.3151:
As soon as she handed the yakisoba bread to me, she quickly
returned to the classroom.
messages.3249: "(You don't have to go so fast...)"
messages.3294:
After all that, I was going to ask to eat together, but I
couldn't call her out before she left.
messages.3397:
Well, for better or for worse... there's no doubt that she's
a kind person.
messages.3665: On my way to buy bread, I bumped into Tamaki.
messages.3729:
She was coming back from buying bread herself. According to
her, it's probably all sold out by now.
messages.3805:
Seeing my crestfallen state, Tamaki insisted on giving me
part of hers, no strings attached.
messages.3897: She's a little weird, but she's definitely a kind person.

messages.153:
There was no real reason to go there, but in the end, I
thought it was a good idea to check on it's condition.
messages.239: I wasn't looking to create trouble or anything.
messages.284:
But since Miharu wasn't around, and we'd actually met, I
wanted to try to get closer to her.
messages.374: Of course, I was talking about Tsukishiro Alice.
messages.409:
Thinking that maybe she may not be here at this time, I
furtively approached the spot.
messages.471:
But, as my view became clearer and clearer, so did the
figure of Tsukishiro.
messages.572: The tiny Tsukishiro snapped her head towards me.
messages.689:
"I can understand it needing water during lunch break at
noon, but what are you doing here after school?"
messages.767:
Squirming, she once again removed her gloves and brought the
doll's head to face me.
messages.842:
Her innocence and purity were reflected in her eyes, as she
gazed at me.
messages.867: She didn't look comfortable at all.
messages.911:
"If we don't watch out here after school, that old janitor
will come around and rip the plant out!"
messages.997:
"...So, you're gonna stay there the whole time, doing
nothing but staring at it?"
messages.1087:
"We don't know when or whether that old guy will come!! We
can't just let it happen."
messages.1165:
"...Tell him when he comes, then leave. You can't stay here
forever."
messages.1318: Her eyes continued piercing into my very soul.
messages.1363: Looks like she hasn't noticed it at all.
messages.1400:
The said part-time janitor was already walking around,
pulling out the weeds around the campus.
messages.1575: I ran up to the janitor, and started explaining.
messages.1649: "He understands not to tear that plant out now."
messages.1733: "...I thought I was supposed to go talk to him."
messages.1774:
"Uh, you mean, letting this doll talk to him? He'd run off
screaming in terror first."
messages.1856:
Not that I'm calling myself Mr. Congeniality, but I'm at
least human.
messages.2025:
"Anyway, it should be alright even if you don't stare at it
24-7 now."
messages.2091:
In this deserted area, only that janitor would think of
encroaching this restricted space anyway.
messages.2236:
"We don't know what might happen... we'd continue keeping
watch for a bit longer."
messages.2300:
As both Tsukishiro and Piros finished talking, they went
back to boring holes into the plant with their eyes.
messages.2386: Seems like no one can stop them.
messages.2431:
Tsukishiro continued squatting next to the plant, showing no
signs of movement at all.
messages.2468:
If it wasn't for her occasional blinking, you'd think that
what she was carrying wasn't the only doll around.
messages.2577:
"Are you really going to keep watching over it? It's going
to get dark soon, you know?"
messages.2639:
Coldness had started to creep in the air, and the sun was
starting to fall behind the clouds; it was time to head
back.
messages.2752: "Our houses are close, why don't we go home together?"
messages.2801: I'm starting to get the shivers, sheesh!
messages.2863: Her skin even looks as white as snow...
messages.2906:
That tiny body can't possibly stand up so long to the
freezing winds of the end of Feburary...
messages.3058:
She suddenly stood up, taking the bag beside her, and ran
off.
messages.3169: By the time I noticed, she'd all but disappeared.
messages.3211:
I tried to chase after her, but the speed at which she ran
made her uncatchable.
messages.3293: She's far more agile than I tbought.
messages.3320: Her figure raced into the Sakura Park opposite the gym,
messages.3414: but by the time I reached there, she had vanished.
messages.3525:
Slowing down to catch my breath, the surroundings were
completely silent besides my panting.
messages.3597: "Oh well, I'd buy a chocolate banana and head back."
messages.3646: Better head home before I catch a cold.
messages.3851:
Visting the gym rear, I found Tsukishiro staring intently at
the flower there.
messages.3923:
Apparently, she was afraid some passerby would rip it out,
thinking it was a weed.
messages.4001:
In Tsukishiro's stead, I explained to the janitor to ignore
the plant at the back of the gym.
messages.4071:
Then, I invited Tsukishiro to head back to our homes
together, but she more or less refused...

messages.149:
As I wandered aimlessly around the shopping district, I felt
a knock on my shoulder.
messages.279:
"Not really... I actually have a painfully detailed schedule
of which places I loiter at, by the minute."
messages.456: Right after Suginami came Kudou, smiling wryly.
messages.531:
"Asakura, how about a game of air hockey? We haven't played
that in a long time."
messages.644: I don't feel like moving around a lot~.
messages.709: "Hmm, another "how troublesome" from you, I bet?"
messages.752:
Suginami grinned widely at me. His words somehow vexed me,
and I decided to take up his offer.
messages.919:
"Mm, now that's more like a man! Kudou, you're a fair
person. I'd leave the judging to you."
messages.1074:
Being appointed as judge rather abruptly, Kudou looked at us
in surprise.
messages.1138:
"Yeah, since you're a common friend, we can expect complete
impartiality from you."
messages.1250:
"Even so... it's just a game, why are you two so serious
about it?"
messages.1344:
Tsk tsk tsk, Suginami and I waved our fingers at Kudou in
perfect unison.
messages.1438:
"You don't understand. A true man treats everything he does
seriously!"
messages.1612:
"Haah... one time cool as ice, another hot-blooded. I'd
never understand you two."
messages.1692:
He released a long sigh as we dragged him to the game
center.
messages.1960: Suginami challenged me to a battle of air hockey.
messages.2044:
Once that was decided, we dragged Kudou along with us to the
game center, forcing him to be our judge.

messages.129:
"(Why do I always feel like sleeping during the afternoon
classes...)"
messages.197:
It was Literature class. The teacher was trying to elaborate
on the mentality and feelings of the characters in some
legend.
messages.269:
Of course, knowing the feelings of some book's character
isn't going to be of much use in the future.
messages.329:
This class would be more centered on trying to increase our
capability of reading and understanding literature...
messages.606: I "sleepstudy" my way through the literature class.

messages.325:
Encountering a crazy goat, being bumped into by Nanako and
getting her important things devoured...
messages.360: This'd never have happened if that stupid goat didn't exist.
messages.430:
I suddenly recalled a copy of "Nuu" that I borrowed form
Suginami awhile ago...
messages.498:
It had a special feature on white and black magic, and the
symbol representing evilness, was a goat.
messages.607:
I couldn't help comparing the likeness of the two images
before my eyes...
messages.675: A cold shiver ran down my spine.
messages.718: "Grr... I should look into ways to exorcise it."
messages.765:
My feet headed to the direction of the only shrine on this
island.
messages.858:
The busiest period of shinto shrines is obviously the new
year.
messages.905:
But even besides that, even a small shrine like this usually
gets quite a few worshippers.
messages.971: It was odd to see only one other person around, like now.
messages.1152: Her face was questioning why I was here, just like my own.
messages.1311:
Taking a closer look, she was holding it close to her chest,
indeed.
messages.1375: I can't read what was written on it.
messages.1414:
Well, I'm not the kind to sneakily invade other people's
privacy, but...
messages.1474:
"Votive picture...? You mean the kind you make a wish on?
What kind of wish did you make?"
messages.1619:
"Wahhh! D, don't look! I, if other people see the wish, it
won't, be, be granted..."
messages.1742: "...I don't remember hearing that about votive pictures."
messages.1817: "W, well, no, but I don't want you to looook..."
messages.1879:
She held it even tighter to her body, turning her back to
me.
messages.1935:
"Oh well, okay. If you don't want me to know so much, I
don't really want to know either."
messages.2049: "Thank you... what about you, what are you doing here...?"
messages.2254: "You can do that in a shrine?"
messages.2299:
"That's what I came here to find out. If God is indeed
almighty, I'm sure he could do it."
messages.2381: Although, I don't know much about the God they worship here.
messages.2570:
Accompanied by Nanako, we passed through the front of the
shrine, and started walking within the grounds.
messages.2675: "Oh yeah, isn't she from your class?"
messages.2771:
"That priestess transfer student I've been eharing so much
about."
messages.2873: "What kind of person do you think she is?"
messages.2978: She was a little outrageous at certain times, but.
messages.3019:
The biggest question was, why she just announced to everyone
that I was her fiancee, like that.
messages.3124:
I spoke vaguely, while racking my brain for a good
description.
messages.3169: "To put it in a single word, she's--"
messages.3276: Nanako and I turned towards the direction of the voice.
messages.3368: She wore a elegant Miko robe, with a scarlet Hakama.
messages.3413:
No matter how you look at it, she resembled the complete
Miko.
messages.3538: She bowed politely. Her eyes then strayed to my side.
messages.3634: "Might you be a friend of Asakura-sama's?"
messages.3761: Nanako's eyes were glittering as they stared at Tamaki.
messages.3819: Tamaki's words didn't penetrate her trance.
messages.3907:
With a slightly flustered face, she called out to Nanako
again.
messages.4007: "Haah, eh...? Ahh! I did it again..."
messages.4080:
"My name is Konomiya Tamaki. You would be a friend of
Asakura-sama's, right?"
messages.4180:
"Ah, yes. A lot kinda happened this morning, but being
friends would be a good way to put it..."
messages.4301: Nanako stole a glance at me.
messages.4472:
With a smile, she removed her glasses, wiping them with her
handkerchief.
messages.4562:
"Then, I'm a friend of Asakura-kun's, Saitama Nanako. Nice
to meet you."
messages.4760: "Did the two of you come to pray today?"
messages.4838:
In the end, I couldn't really tell her that I was here to
exorcise a demon goat.
messages.5067:
...Or so I thought, as she suddenly whirled around to face
us.
messages.5141:
"By the way, it would be preferred if you walk at the sides
of the path."
messages.5243: Tamaki smiled lightly as she explained.
messages.5279:
"In past times, the peasants would walk to the sides, so as
not to interfere with the Gods walking through the middle."
messages.5473:
As she spoke, Nanako took out a pen and something else from
her pocket.
messages.5549:
Muttering "I see..." to herself, she started scribbling
furiously.
messages.5674:
"Gyahh! N, nothing! I was just thinking, hearing such a
ancient custom, that I had to make a memo of it..."
messages.5783: That was way more surprise than was needed, Nanako.
messages.5882:
Nanako shoved the memo pad back into her pocket, trying to
laugh it off.
messages.5959:
She was probably a little put off by Tamaki as well, looking
dignified in her element.
messages.6136: Tamaki set off, with us following. A cool wind blew past us.
messages.6229: After a short walk, we reached the hall of worship.
messages.6295: "The offering place for votive pictures is over there."
messages.6344:
Tamaki pointed to the side of the hall of worship, where
several votive pictures like Nanako's hung.
messages.6464: Nanako dashed over to that area, like a little kid.
messages.6542:
I wasn't really serious in thinking that I had to exorcise
that "demon goat" out of me.
messages.6630:
It's far more likely for that goat to be a simple domestic
animal rather than a tool of Satan.
messages.6764:
I walked up the stairs of the hall of worship, stopping in
front of the offertory box.
messages.6809: "(I better not fool around with Tamaki watching.)"
messages.6893:
Throwing a 5 yen coin inside, I waited for the sound of the
coin hitting the bottom of the box, and bowed.
messages.6963:
I clasped my hands together, and started to state my name
and wish, in my mind.
messages.7051:
"(I don't have much to wish for, but please protect me from
misfortune... oh, and please keep Nemu in good health.)"
messages.7207: For one last time, I bowed towards the hall of worship.
messages.7290: Nanako had returned from her own business too.
messages.7361:
"I still have matters to attend to at the shrine office, so
I shall take my leave."
messages.7443: With a bow, she slowly left.
messages.7496: As she disappeared from our view, Nanako sighed softly.
messages.7595:
"Konomiya-san's amazing... she's so pretty and composed,
it's hard to believe we're the same age."
messages.7724: "Her Miko clothes are so authentic as well."
messages.7833:
Especially to be able to ignore crowds and shoot arrows
right in the middle...
messages.7942:
But really, she has the looks, smarts, intelligence, even
sportiness.
messages.8061:
Why would a girl as perfect as that, call herself my
fiancee? That's a real puzzle.
messages.8135:
"(Suginami would immediately suspect alien conspiracies, for
sure...)"
messages.8216: I then noticed that Nanako was staring at me.
messages.8457: With dusk quickly approaching, we left the shrine.
messages.8676:
After school, I thought of the many misfortunes that befell
me today. I wanted to exorcise the demon goat that attacked
me.
messages.8793:
Heading to the only shrine on Hatsu-nejima, I found Nanako,
with a votive picture.
messages.8851:
While talking to Nanako, Tamaki found and brought us in,
teaching us about some of the etiquette used within the
shrine.
messages.8929:
Nanako was enamoured with the miko costume-clad Tamaki, the
person who called herself my fiancee...
messages.9033: We left the shrine at the coming of dusk.

messages.176:
Walking around idly around the Sakura Park, I happened upon
what seemed like a playground inside.
messages.232: I don't remember seeing this... I think.
messages.267:
No, I have vague memories of this place, but not actually
coming here...
messages.414: Nothing for me to do here anyway.
messages.443:
Although there's no kids around right now, I don't really
feel like playing around.
messages.537:
Well, maybe one day when I get the urge to re-live my
childhood...
messages.771: I don't remember it being there though...

messages.196: I saw a familiar hat in a queue for a food cart.
messages.489:
Her face lit up upon recognizing me. Somehow, her smile is
so infectious.
messages.610:
The front of the line is too far from here to see exactly
what's being sold.
messages.706: "Yes. My stomach was rumbling, and it was on the way, so..."
messages.770:
Kotori's quite famous around Kazami Academy. A lot of people
call her the "School Idol".
messages.858:
But just looking at her queueing up to buy food, she looks
like a perfectly normal girl.
messages.1028:
"Never heard of it? It's like a big piece of meat with a
stick pierced through it, then spun around constantly over a
fire..."
messages.1112:
"...And it's usually eaten on a piece of bread, with
vegetables in between."
messages.1212: "...I won't be able to eat something so filling now."
messages.1346:
"Recently, a vendor selling delicious crepes has started
coming around this park. It's famous around the school."
messages.1542:
While talking about that, Kotori's turn at the vendor
quickly came up.
messages.1730: "Alright, Asakura-kun, please take one. The treat's on me."
messages.1806: With a quick bow, I take one of the crepes.
messages.1968: Kotori was carrying a crepe in each hand.
messages.2060: "Ahh, I'd be eating both of these."
messages.2122: That would be about as filling as a Donel Kebab.
messages.2208: "...You think this would make me fat?"
messages.2337: We found a bench to sit on, and bit into our crepes.
messages.2473:
The sweetness of the crepe filled my tastebuds, and I closed
my eyes in bliss.
messages.2537:
Although it's a bit weird eating such a cold thing in
Feburary, it tastes just as good anytime.
messages.2589:
Besides, even though the air is cold, the sun is still
shining, it's rays showering gently onto the earth.
messages.2659:
"I didn't know you'd eat such a thing though. You've never
said before that you like sweets, have you?"
messages.2762: "I like sweet stuff of all sorts."
messages.2835:
"That's why I'm always thinking of going on a diet, they're
so fattening..."
messages.2916: I do a quick once-over of her with my eyes.
messages.2963: "I don't think you have anything to be worried about."
messages.3008:
She pretty much has the perfect body, with perfect
proportions.
messages.3133:
She muttered, as her face turned red and she looked away in
embarassment.
messages.3289: Said just like some old lady.
messages.3332:
"...Nah, more like you're a slow eater? ...Oh, the crepe's
fillings are oozing out..."
messages.3453:
...If she hadn't noticed the food dripping from her hand,
she'd have to be quite slow...
messages.3599: "Ah, I mean, what you said just now."
messages.3649:
We were talking about Kotori being slow on finshing her
crepe, I nearly forgot.
messages.3709: "Just eat it slowly and enjoy it."
messages.3799: I've already been treated to an ice crepe anyway.
messages.3855: "No, I mean... do you think you can eat one more?"
messages.3986:
The sun's rays were quickly turning the ice crepe into
liquid crepe.
messages.4095:
I tried to prepare my stomach somehow, and took one of the
crepes from Kotori.
messages.4218: "...I won't be able to stomach more than two."
messages.4324: With that, we continued eating the ice crepes together.
messages.4615:
I met Kotori at the Sakura Park, and she treated me to some
ice crepes.
messages.4699: They were great, but such cold stuff in the winter...

messages.240: Slowly savouring her ramen, Nemu was in paradise.
messages.341: "As good as it is, I'm getting sick of Chinese food."
messages.392:
Poking the remnants of my Chinese-style fried rice with my
work, I let out a little sigh.
messages.479:
"I suppose. There's still pizza, take-out, dinner
delivery... how do yo you want to rotate it?"
messages.587:
"No, what I meant was having something different from that
usual menu..."
messages.695: "If that's the case, have fun cooking dinner."
messages.734:
I nearly spit out my after-meal tea, under the scowling gaze
of Nemu.
messages.804:
"If you want me to cook, then don't complain about the
inedibility and cost of ingredients from the result."
messages.910:
"We don't have much money left... so leave the cooking to
me~"
messages.972: Nemu pointed to herself, or more accurately, her nose.
messages.1003: "....In any case, that can wait till after the tests."
messages.1061:
I'd rather pay an assassin to poison my food than taste her
cooking.
messages.1191:
She tilted her head to the side in what looked like an
impossible angle.
messages.1259:
Both ways, I'd have to start preparing my stomach now for
the torture to come...
messages.1310:
"You know, now that I think about it, convenience store food
really does have a large selection..."
messages.1428: Completely ignoring me, Nemu reached for my chopsticks.
messages.1560:
With a little sigh, and with nothing particular to watch on
TV, I went to my room on the second floor.
messages.1889: "What's the fuss about? Did you see a cockroach?"
messages.1936: Nemu's face came peeking out from the kitchen.
messages.1981: "Did we leave any beans from Bean Throwing Night?!"
messages.2140: I ran back up the stairs.
messages.2300:
I picked Sakura up from my bed, and put her on one of the
spare cushions lying around.
messages.2443: "Haa... where on earth did you come in here from?"
messages.2538: "Through the front door, using a key?"
messages.2588:
"By climbing up the sakura tree and through your window.
Didn't you hear me knock?"
messages.2656: Sakura pointed to the window just above the bed.
messages.2693: "...No one in the world would consider that normal."
messages.2762: "You said it would be fine before!"
messages.2805: "Huh? ...Aah, that was back when we were kids."
messages.2863: I fell back into a chair with a sigh.
messages.2896:
Sakura used to climb up the tree near her house to get into
my room to play, as it stretched all the way to my window.
messages.3017: That's right, we used to play well into the night...
messages.3081:
"But, at this age, going into a male's room so casually,
there's a lot of things wrong with that."
messages.3201: "Ah, ehehe. You look ready for that anyway."
messages.3271:
Sakura gave her best impression of a sultry smile, and
started lifting the hem of her skirt.
messages.3364:
Trying not to look, I shook my head from side to side
vigourously.
messages.3464: "What's wrong? Why's your face so red?"
messages.3509: "...Because of all your talk about being "ready"."
messages.3584:
"Psh, I'm wearing bloomers underneath after all. Want to
see?"
messages.3706:
The feeling of gazing at the blue sky is so invigorating...
It washes away the tears of the heart.
messages.3820:
"Aaaah, it would've been so much better if we were in the
same class..."
messages.3884: "...Don't say such terrifying things so easily."
messages.3992: "Don't mind me. Anyway, what did you come here for?"
messages.4056: Some night-viewing of sakura trees, maybe?
messages.4174: "You already made so much fuss about it in school..."
messages.4253:
"Boo! So you still don't want to welcome back someone who
moved away so long ago!"
messages.4325:
Sakura slapped her left knee with her right palm in disgust,
her eyebrows narrowing.
messages.4429:
"You listen! Yoshino Sakura, returning from faraway America,
has finally come back to the unwashed masses!"
messages.4557:
"From now on, I will mingle shoulder-to-shoulder with the
underpriveleged, and eventually take my rightful position at
the top of this mess!"
messages.4762:
"Basically, don't shut your door to someone who's just moved
in next to you♪"
messages.4832: "I don't see why that's a problem."
messages.4884:
"Don't say that~ When duty and personal feelings battle it
out, that duty should win is one of the world's laws-- isn't
it?"
messages.5088:
"What? Are you questioning my Japanese nationality? How
foolish!"
messages.5183: Sakura beat her chest in confidence.
messages.5306: "You're making fun of Japan, arenn't you..."
messages.5343: I point a half-hearted finger at her as I sighed.
messages.5407:
From childhood, she had taken the path of no return, and her
move overseas just further established the fact.
messages.5504:
Sushi, Tempura, Fujiyama... the transition from Japanese to
American appears to have been complete.
messages.5582: "Haah... Is that all you've got to say?"
messages.5652:
"Mmm, I guess. Anyways, I wanted to say, from now on, let's
be good neighbours!"
messages.5732: Still sitting on her cushion, she stuck out three fingers.
messages.5800: "Of course. As long as from now on..."
messages.5841:
From now on, you knock on the door and enter through the
hallway, just like a normal person.
messages.5963:
"Eheheh, that's right, you still haven't fixed the key for
that."
messages.6096: "They key for that window, it broke 6 years ago, remember?"
messages.6141: Grabbing my attention again, Sakura pointed to the window.
messages.6207:
Now that she's said that, Nemu's been insecure about that
and always bothering me to fix that window...
messages.6306: Although, the way I look at it, that's no problem at all.
messages.6360: "...That's because it's troublesome to do so."
messages.6530:
"Yeah, very convenient. Whenever I want to hang out with
you..."
messages.6594:
Sakura stood up and opened the window, then turned her head
around and giggled slightly.
messages.6662:
The cold air blew through, and the scent of sakuras could be
smelt; not a bad feeling at all.
messages.6766: "Hey, can you still make that come out?"
messages.6799:
Sakura stuck out her palm, then opened and closed it a few
times.
messages.6865:
I closed my hand up into a fist, and pictured an appropriate
wagashi--a manjuu, in my head.
messages.6931: Soon enough, my hand started getting a lot heavier.
messages.6993:
--As well as the power to see into dreams, the strange power
to create wagashis--
messages.7075: It really does sound like some strange fairytale.
messages.7110:
It's something that sounds so stupid that only Nemu, and of
course Sakura, knows about it.
messages.7215: "Lots of red bean in this one. Catch!"
messages.7295:
I threw the manjuu in the air, and Sakura, after a bout of
confusion, managed to hold onto it.
messages.7351:
"You better remember to brush your teeth after you eat
that."
messages.7483:
Acting childlike anyway, Sakura stuck out her tongue, then
started heading out the window.
messages.7618:
From the darkness outside the window, I could hear Sakura's
reply.
messages.7687: "Ah... Eheh, it's good to be back~"
messages.7752:
Sakura quickly dropped out the window, her figure
disappearing from sight.
messages.7806:
I could still see her hand grasping the branch of the Sakura
tree.
messages.7843:
Since I was a bit foolhardy in my younger days, the branch
still held the wound of being broken into half.
messages.7931: "That girl... she hasn't changed one bit."
messages.7978:
As the sakura continued fluttering right outside my window,
I went over and shut it.
messages.8191:
After dinner, when I went to my room, Sakura was there. She
didn't come through the door, but instead from the window.
Really, she scared me half to death...
messages.8308:
Sakura came to finagle a "welcome back" out of me. She
managed to come in through the window, since it's lock has
been broken for the last 6 years.
messages.8411:
After a bit of reminscience, she went out the same way she
came in.
messages.8491:
The sakura tree branch outside which she used to climb,
thanks to my clumsiness before, was torn quite badly.
messages.8559: That Sakura... she really hasn't changed one bit.

messages.150:
I read a manga while resting my head on my bolster. Next
door, I can hear Sakura's shrill voice every now and then.
messages.269: Even alone, she can make so much noise.
messages.342:
I reach out to the alarm clock and set the alarm for
tomorrow.
messages.470: After setting the alarm, I continued studying.
messages.528: After setting the alarm, I continued studying.
messages.577: After setting the alarm, I slept.
messages.746:
I figured it was the right time to sleep once Sakura next
door actually quietened down for once.
messages.855: Time to set the alarm clock, then.

messages.197: I closed my eyelids, and relaxed my body...

messages.166: "There's no announcements today, so I'd end HR now."
messages.222: As she left the classroom, the weekly duty quickly stood up.
messages.332:
With just the announcement from the weekly duty, today's HR
ended as soon as it started.
messages.396: "Now then... how will I go back today."
messages.443: I stretch my arms above my head as I question myself.
messages.637:
After school, Koyomi-sensei started the HR session and
immediately said that she'd end it.

messages.306:
Today wasn't very different. A normal morning routine of
waking up, breakfast, measuring Nemu's temperature...
messages.443:
"I never thought I'd see the day where I'd have to say
"Nii-san, wait up!"..."
messages.537: She pretended to wipe away tears, mocking me further.
messages.582: "...Excuuuse me. You've said that plenty of times to me."
messages.682:
"...That's true. Like when that time when you stole my
afternoon snack, or at the zoo when you tried to ditch me at
the playpen...
messages.813: "You have a memory like an elephant..."
messages.858: Clicking my tongue, I answered her back.
messages.915: "Of course, it has to do with you after all."
messages.956:
Her reply was in the same manner, down to the action. How
many times have people fallen to that terrifying face...
messages.1061: "From now on, please let me say that in a good way instead."
messages.1187:
Sheesh, I wake up early for once, and I get this treatment.
Makes me not want to get up early at all.
messages.1259:
Glancing to the side, I saw a briskly-walking figure easing
past us.
messages.1340:
Her pretty, fluttering hair came to a halt at the sound of
my voice.
messages.1396: "Morning. I wasn't expecting to meet you here."
messages.1517: A barely audible voice as usual.
messages.1546:
"So you go to school at this time? Looks like we can walk to
school toget..."
messages.1631:
Before I could complete my sentence, Tsukishiro had
completely overtaken us and continued her brisk walk to
school.
messages.1784:
"Nii-san, who was that girl? She seemed like a second year
student..."
messages.1844:
"Mm? Ah, yeah. I found and returned her student notebook a
few days ago."
messages.1948:
"Hmm, I see. How unusual for you to make acquaintances so
easily."
messages.2028: "What do you mean by unusual, huh?"
messages.2079: Besides, the one that's unusual is... Tsukishiro, really.
messages.2133:
The strange doll she carries, her foreign appearance, and
those mysterious eyes always staring at something...
messages.2232:
And staying in that huge mansion, with a butler at her
service...
messages.2475: "I called out to you so many times."
messages.2594: Nemu puffed her cheeks in exasperation.
messages.2633: "Come on, don't give me that kind of face. Let's go."
messages.2676: I suddenly stepped up my walking speed.
messages.2715:
There's no point waking up this early, only to walk like a
slug to school.
messages.2854: Saying those magic words, Nemu started chasing after me.
messages.3081: I unusually woke up early, and accompanied Nemu to school.
messages.3133:
En-route, we bumped into Tsukishiro, who whispered a simple
"Good morning" and hurried off to school.
messages.3254: I don't think she was being rude, but...

messages.377: Sleepy... I couldn't have set the alarm this early..
messages.475:
I opened my eyes into slits, and searched for the snooze
button on the alarm clock.
messages.529:
I hit the snooze button, then turn over and try to sleep
again.
messages.597: Beside me and right in front of my eyes, I saw a face.
messages.667:
My drowziness wore off in an instant as I jumped up in
horror.
messages.690: Lying on my futon was Sakura, clad only in her pajamas.
messages.795:
I try to calm myself down, and recall the events of the
night before.
messages.847: I don't remember anything about this before I fell asleep.
messages.888:
"(Don't tell me, another unauthorized intrusion from the
window?)"
messages.921: Whatever the case, I can't let Nemu see this.
messages.1046: Sakura was still half-asleep, and replied in a dreamy voice.
messages.1093:
"Come on, hurry up and wake up! Go back out through the
window again!"
messages.1163:
I forcefully sit her up, and shake her shoulders
vigourously.
messages.1253: Sakura finally opened her massive eyelids.
messages.1378: "Don't just greet me normally! Why're you sleeping here?"
messages.1452: I poke Sakura's sleepy face in the forehead.
messages.1589:
"Anyway, wake up already and go back to your house through
the window! If Nemu sees this, she'd kill me!"
messages.1770: I turn to face Sakura, and see her usual grin.
messages.1854:
"Then I'd leave now. If I'm around, Nemu will be maaad
right?"
messages.1934: "That's why I said, hurry up and go!"
messages.2036:
She lightly jumped out the window, and standing on the
branch, turned back and gave a little wave before
disappearing out of sight.
messages.2175:
With one hand on my chest and one in my hair, I head to the
bathroom to wash my face.
messages.2422:
Waken up by the alarm, somehow, Sakura was sleeping beside
me. Just why did she come here now...
messages.2514: I quickly woke her up, and chased her out of my room.

messages.149:
There are only three places in Kazami Academy that I have
never set foot in.
messages.213:
The girl's bathroom, the girl's locker room, and the
library.
messages.256:
Well, more accurately, if I don't have a specific reason to
go there, I never will.
messages.330:
Of course, for the first two, there's absolutely no reason
for me to enter.
messages.377:
But there is for the last. For example, when I need to take
a lunchtime nap.
messages.416:
However, this time, my reason for going there was slightly
different--
messages.547: "Nii-san, could you...? I can't bring these over by myself."
messages.598: "The dictionaries we used for fourth period?"
messages.683: "There isn't anyone else you can ask?"
messages.760:
"Well... look at Murasaki-san for yourself, do you think she
could? I don't have the heart to ask her."
messages.861:
"You should pay for your own mistakes. You knew you weren't
going to be able to do it, yet volunteered so eagerly for
it."
messages.973:
"That's true, but... well, then what do you think I should
do?"
messages.1102:
"Letting your adorable sister collapse due to too much hard
labour, what would our family think..."
messages.1188:
"...Okay, okay, I got it. Just take these to the library,
right?"
messages.1303: "...Then why did I end up carrying all of them!?"
messages.1354: In the end, I was a substitute more than a helper.
messages.1428:
I slowly started to place the 20 dictionaries back on their
respective shelves.
messages.1482: She owes me one hell of a take-out for this tonight...
messages.1544:
I looked around, and noticed a familiar-looking female
sitting at a desk, and reading a book. ...It's Tsukishiro.
messages.1632:
Even while wearing the black gloves, she skillfully brushed
past each page.
messages.1688: The book she was reading was nothing short of huge.
messages.1742: The usual doll was sitting quietly in her lap.
messages.1816:
Noticing my shadow falling onto her book, she gazed up at
me.
messages.1937:
She removed her hand from over the book, to reveal a piece
of paper with a rough sketch of a plant on it.
messages.2066:
"So that's what you're looking at... I guess regarding the
plant behind the gym?"
messages.2186: "You mean, you don't know that plant's name?"
messages.2237: A shake of the head no, this time.
messages.2285:
"Then, you're trying to find out how to take care of it
properly?"
messages.2364:
"Ehhnn... it's hard to talk like this, maybe you should get
your doll to talk again like before."
messages.2479: She then took a look around the library.
messages.2506: I did the same as well.
messages.2552:
Nothing out of the ordinary. Just a few people quietly
reading books, and a couple of people scribbling furiously
with pencils.
messages.2712:
But after her surveying, she sadly shook her head towards
me.
messages.2831:
Returning her eyes to her book, she resumed her vigilant
reading.
messages.2905:

encyclopedia.

I tried to talk to her about various things, but I couldn't

lunch.

......It's pretty good once in a while to spend a lunch
break thinking to yourself.

familiar.

ganmodoki.

I shook my head in light disbelief asn I opened my bread
packet.

The three of us, chewing on our food, were interrupted by

Three rascals hiding behind the gym produces this kind of
situation now?

"It feels like an open-air cafe in Daikan'yama, an elegant

"Hm... regrettable. I thought we were three bachelors of

there.

Eventually, we talked about random little nothings as lunch

Muffled voices could be heard from students, an ordinary
school morning.

attendance, Koyomi quickly left the classroom.

I shouldn't show my ignorance at something she's obviously

Rather than talking about mindless things, I should just try

"Well, if you don't want to talk about it, fine... but if

But it looks like saying what it is would really be too much

"What comes to your mind, when you think about the duties of

messages.4449:
"There is also the maintenance of the shrine area, and the

"Before festivals begin, we are also required to perform a

Man, Miko have it pretty tough. They're definitely not just

"H, hey, could I have a glimpse of that dance you

My imagination started running, with the thought of a male

Dancing like that in full public view, that'd be way too

Tamaki had to concentrate on her cleaning to finish it, so I

In the end, I didn't know any more about our supposed

I headed to the shrine, and found Tamaki sweeping the stone

While having a cup of tea with her, I found out why she

The chief priest's health had deteroriated, so her family

I yawned and stretch my back, sitting cross-legged on my

As I take a glance at him, he was wearing the same

Kudou's around, talking with Tahata. Reticient as ever,

messages.560:
Nemu... being a disciplinary club member, of course she's

Shigeru's here. Kakuta... isn't here yet. Poor guy, he'd be

Right in front of my eyes, the pink bear-- something you'd

I turn to face Suginami and answer him with a smile. What I

"Ahh, nothing's wrong, nothing at all. Right, I'd go to the

I headed for the exit of the classroom, making sure not to

"Occasionally, it is a fine idea to deepen our

That's right, what I saw just now must definitely have been

Steeling my mind on that idea-- no, truth, my heart felt a

messages.2400:
Surely my heart will be able to keep beating for the rest of

"Just kidding. You're still young, you won't tire from that

"I told you I was joking! Although truthfully, you don't

"Nevermind... what I'm seeing now is too crazy for anyone to

"What are you talking about? Do you remember who you're

"Of course! Even if you've heard something or seen something

"Even if you told me that aliens were overrunning this

Thank goodness... at least in these times, Suginami's a

"The truth is... there's a bear in the classroom right

"You just said you'd surely understand and believe my

I close my eyes and rub them again. As I open them, I pray

As I continue staring at the pink bear and it's school

Right now, I have to believe in what I feel in my heart!

messages.4844:
But, really, this does seem to be reality... no, it is

No one else seems to be bothered by it, and it's definitely

messages.5075:
Then I might as well take the iniatiative and participate

I bet everyone else is too shy to unless someone else does

"...You should tell the teacher that you need to go to the

Maybe... I'm the weird one? I'm the one who's acting

I have to be fine... yet everyone else doesn't see it. How

messages.6187:
Maybe if I investigate that bear, everything will be

I rushed up to the back of the bear, and jabbed my finger

"Why're you wearing a bear costume in school?! It is a

Once again, I said something incredibly stupid before I

"Brother... at the very least, don't throw away what

I tried to explain myself, but cut myself short. I'm really

Everyone around me was staring at me with pitiful contempt

There is a bear. It is wearing clothes. No one else has

Koyomi-sensei had entered the classroom, banging the

Like a bunch of spiders scattering back to their webs, my

Everyone else must be deceiving me. Surely the teacher can

What on earth is going on here? There's definitely a pink

Yet the class was completely unaware, as was the teacher,

Everything I remembered about her has been replaced by a

messages.11019:
I thought aloud, and stood up from my desk. The bear was

messages.11139:
"Yoshita, Yonesawa... there's nothing weird, Asakura! If
