can't picture the human Murasaki in my mind.
messages.13359:
Why can't I even remember this supposedly normal-looking
phantom? It must be some fault of my mood right now...
messages.13464:
Maybe after I take a good rest here, I can clear my head and
maybe stop stubornly claiming that I can see a bear...
messages.13571: Daaah! I can't sleep just yet!
messages.13637: If I do, I'd completely forget what happened just now.
messages.13715:
I did something pretty bad to Murasaki... I did try to take
off her clothes, after all.
messages.13793: I have to apologize to her soon.
messages.13826:
Yet I still can't forget the soft and fluffy feel of fur on
my hand...
messages.13896:
Still lying on the futon in the nurse's office, I let on a
large yawn.
messages.13966: From outside my blanket, I heard Nemu sigh.
messages.14086: I heard a timid voice through the blanket.
messages.14180:
"Ah, Murasaki... Sorry about earlier. I don't know what I
was thinking... but I honestly wasn't trying to hurt you.
messages.14309:
I made a heartfelt apology, but didn't have the guts to face
her.
messages.14390: "Aya, I'm fine with it... please don't worry about that."
messages.14487: I finally uncover my face from the blanket.
messages.14543: Ance once I did, in front of my eyes was--
messages.14654: Yet again, I saw the pink bear.
messages.14767:
We simultaneously recoil in a combination of surprise and
horror.
messages.14812:
I calm myself, straight my posture, blink my eyes a few
times... and that freaking bear is still there.
messages.14972: The bear gave a quick nod.
messages.15031: "Uhm... Asakura-san, do you see me as a bear?"
messages.15150: "Um, about that, please don't tell anyone else about it..."
messages.15206: The bear bowed in polite request.
messages.15241:
"...You mean, that your real figure is really that of a
bear?..."
messages.15337:
"Ya... the truth is, there's a good reason for this... why
I'm wearing clothes, and why you see me as a bear..."
messages.15509: "The reason? ...Please don't make me tell the reason..."
messages.15571: The bear hung it's head in shame, fidgeting nervously.
messages.15625:
"Well... It's not like I'd tell anyone else. What's wrong
with explaining this whole thing to me?"
messages.15722:
"But if I do, you probably won't understand or believe
me..."
messages.15784:
"Isn't the fact that I've accepted this bear standing in
front of me enough proof that I would?"
messages.15898:
"So would it be okay to tell me? This is pretty weird after
all."
messages.15976:
Although this island is pretty notorious for weird
occurrences, this one must beat them all easily.
messages.16092: "Well... please don't laugh or get mad..."
messages.16166:
"I won't get mad. Unless you say you're some alien doing
scouting for an invsaion or something."
messages.16268:
"Ayaya... looks like there's no need for me to say
anything."
messages.16343:
"Why not? I said I won't get mad... unless you mean you're
really some alien planning on kidnapping our cattle and
humans."
messages.16472: I start guffawing at my own joke, if only so someone would.
messages.16546: I didn't expect her to fall for it so well.
messages.16664:
"It, it's not about that... it's the Galaxy Federation's
plan to prevent uncivilized planets from being forcefully
colonized..."
messages.16815:
"We don't have the time or motivation to do any kidnapping
or live experiments or anything like that..."
messages.16963:
It worried me quite a bit that she's taking my joke about
invasion and kidnapping far more seriously than I expected.
messages.17067:
I wasn't exactly expecting any sort of reply for a horrible
joke like that.
messages.17158:
"That is... the reason I'm currently staying on this planet.
I mean no harm whatsoever..."
messages.17263: "Um...? Murasaki-san, can you tell me one thing?"
messages.17422:
"Ah... about 820 light years away from Earth, the 4th planet
of the Kilito Star System, Sheem."
messages.17546:
Another serious reply to a lighthearted question... wait,
don't tell me...
messages.17696: "As you can see... yes I am."
messages.17743: "So there really is an earth invasion..."
messages.17791:
"Aya, I told you earlier, there's no real worth in invading
Earth anyway, so..."
messages.17890:
A weird island, a weird grandmother, weird powers, so many
strange things...
messages.17950:
Yet no matter how many of those strange things I've
experienced, I can't say I've ever met an alien before.
messages.18038:
Suginami's a alien fanatic, so he's talked a lot about these
things, although I've rarely listened to him.
messages.18096:
But I would've figured the first contact would be some form
of galaxy-wide peace announcement or something...
messages.18211:
Instead, the first contact... is with a single alien which
apparently looks like a bear.
messages.18283:
"Err, can you provide any proof to show that you're really
an alien?"
messages.18431: "...Nevermind, sorry. It was a stupid question."
messages.18485:
The very fact that this bear stands before me cannot be
explained by earthly means.
messages.18543:
Despite the completely insane-sounding situation under any
other circumstances, at this point, it's not sounding as
far-fetched anymore...
messages.18645: "So anyway, why am I seeing you as a bear?"
messages.18733:
"Well, originally, to prevent confusion and chaos, I
temporarly took the place of a human. That human was
Murasaki Izumiko."
messages.18853:
"The people around me treated me just the same as if I was
really her."
messages.18909:
"Well, I honestly have no idea why, but I've completely
forgotten what Murasaki looks like anymore, or anything like
that..."
messages.19027:
"I'm clueless as well. Possibly the machine had a breakdown
or something..."
messages.19097:
"But really... I'm meeting a non-earthling intelligent life
form for the first time, and it's some toy-like bear-type
alien..."
messages.19226:
In my mind, I was imagining some Grey-type alien, the kind
that would want to invade and take over the earth. Instead,
I get this.
messages.19389:
"Uhm, I'm not exactly a "bear-type alien" or anything like
that..."
messages.19508:
"In my present state, my condition would deteriorate quickly
if I was exposed to this atmosphere... so I wear a space
suit..."
messages.19629:
I look up and down Murasaki's figure, licking my lips
unconsciously.
messages.19719: "Aya... don't stare at me so carefully like that..."
messages.19781:
Murasaki, having a bout of self-consciousness, tried somehow
to hide herself.
messages.19901: "Ayaya... I'm not a bear, I'm not a bear~!"
messages.19971:
The bear waved her large, bright pink hand around
frantically.
messages.20071:
"...in any case, Asakura-san, do you now believe everything
I've said?"
messages.20161:
"What you said just now? I'm more or less used to weird
phenomena anwyay. Now that I know this, I feel more relaxed
than anything."
messages.20289:
The truth is, whether she's an alien or some subeterranean,
I'm really glad anyway.
messages.20361: Whether she's really an alien or not,
messages.20410:
the very fact that I'm not hallucinating about giant pink
bears existing randomly is enough for me.
messages.20511:
Well, there's no proof that I'm not hallucinating and she's
not lying to me, but her explanation sounds reasonable
enough.
messages.20599:
It's something I can agree with anyway, so that's good
enough.
messages.20663:
Yet inside me, I know that this Murasaki is quite an
enigma...
messages.20721: "But... why does it... heh heh... have to look like that?"
messages.20805:
It's a bit hard to be serious about talking to a giant pink
bear.
messages.20897: Not to mention wearing those clothes on top of that...
messages.20991:
"Aya... it couldn't be helped. I needed to find some
clothes, so I copied that which I saw on an animal..."
messages.21182:
"Well, we don't really have much information on this
uncivilized planet, so clothing information is scarce as
well..."
messages.21262: Murasaki gave a light apology with her words.
messages.21301:
I guess she doesn't think much of the earth in the large
scale of things.
messages.21391:
"Ah, now that I remember, look at this! This outfit is
pretty useful, there's a function within the fingernail of
the hands..."
messages.21502:
While saying that, Murasaki skillfully opened the fingernail
of one of her fingers.
messages.21641:
At the very tip of her fingernail, a bunch of candies were
rolling around...
messages.21712: "This is really handy for when I get hungry!"
messages.21799:
Right here, right now, is the start of an inter-galactic
war. At least, that's what I thought, as I took one of the
candies.
messages.21932:
"In any case, Asakura-san, I'm heading back to the
classroom."
messages.21981:
"Okay. Don't worry about what you've said today. I won't
tell anyone anything, now that I've understood."
messages.22113:
If I tell anyone that I have a bear for a classmate, they'd
just laugh at me anyway.
messages.22199:
"But, since I've come to earth, this is the first time I've
told anyone about this entire thing. It makes me feel
relieved..."
messages.22306:
"That's understandable. And besides, myself as an earthling,
I'm happy to be able to meet people from other planets."
messages.22439: After saying that, Murasaki silently left the infirmary.
messages.22526:
Really though, meeting an alien... that has to be pretty
damn strange, even by my standards.
messages.22594:
No no, I'm already used to strange things, this isn't a rare
thing for me.
messages.22670: I make a Karintou in my hand, and throw it in my mouth.
messages.22732: As always, a completely useless power.
messages.22765: I guess now I'd have to sleep for two periods...
messages.22990:
In the morning, as I entered my classroom, somehow, I saw a
pink bear.
messages.23060:
One of those things that look like they belong in an
amusement park.
messages.23103:
But I was the only one who saw it. Everyone else saw the
usual classmate, Murasaki Izumiko.
messages.23204:
I got a bit too heated up about the subject, and was sent to
the infirmary.
messages.23268:
After a while, the bear came and confessed that she was
actually an alien...
messages.23354: She then explained to me the rest of her secrets.

messages.203: I was early for school today, for once.
messages.252:
With enough time on my hands, I decide to walk to school and
avoid the crowds on the bus.
messages.480:
"This is a pretty rare sight, seeing you here walking so
calmly at this time."
messages.589:
I turned my head over my shoulder to answer her. It's not
surprising that she thinks that, I suppose.
messages.661:
No matter how many times I'm early for school now, it won't
be easy to shake the title of "Lateness King" off my
reputation.
messages.777:
"Anyway, my friends are waiting for me up ahead, so I'd make
a move."
messages.871:
That Kotori, with her cheerful style, light voice and ready
smile... it's always enough to brighten up someone's day.
messages.1003: "This is rare, Asakura. You're going to make it rain now."
messages.1054: A light punch on my shoulder followed the words.
messages.1113:
"Oh, it's just you Kudou. As biting as ever even this early
in the morning, huh?"
messages.1182: "It's the truth, this doesn't happen often at all."
messages.1241: "Well, it won't do to be late anyway."
messages.1297:
We started walking towards the school, participating in
thoughtless morning chatter.
messages.1365: This is a pretty new experience for me...
messages.1398:
Not to mention there's some oddly sweet smell in the morning
air...
messages.1521:
"Hm? Scent? Sorry, must've been from the morning bath I
took."
messages.1583:
Kudou ran his thumb and index finger through his hair a few
times.
messages.1651:
"Well, it's okay I guess. Nemu always takes morning showers
as well."
messages.1735:
That's pretty typical of a girl, and I've never followed her
example.
messages.1791:
But having enough time to linger around and enjoy a bath
makes me feel sort of envious.
messages.1859: Maybe I should consider waking up earlier to do so...
messages.2076:
Tsukishiro actually saying something to me doesn't happen
very often... I'm glad she did, though.
messages.2161:
--Then, before I could even continue the "conversation",
Tsukishiro had already walked right past and moved in front
of me.
messages.2353:
I felt a bit sad just leaving it as "knowing her", but it's
a bit too much to call her a friend right now.
messages.2547: "But, why's she holding that doll with her..."
messages.2609: "Ahh, Tsukishiro has a knack for ventriloquism."
messages.2701:
I don't even know whether it's really ventriloquism... but
it's too early to say something like "the doll can actually
talk".
messages.2908: "Heyy, that laugh sounded like it implied something."
messages.3016:
Although he said that, it's obvious he was thinking about
something involving a close friendship between senpai and
kouhai*...
messages.3117: Of course the situation isn't like that.
messages.3164: But he somehow got that idea, I bet...
messages.3243: "Yo, guys. The weather is superb today!"
messages.3319:
Suddenly, Suginami appeared from between us, seperating our
shoulders with his hands.
messages.3426:
After the usual morning greeting, the three of us continued
our way down the avenue.
messages.3478: Along the way, we also passed by Mako and said hello.
messages.3556:
From this morning, I started thinking that maybe going to
school on time isn't bad after all.
messages.3624: I should get up early more often.
messages.3853:
On a rare occasion when I woke up early, I met Kotori and
Kudou on the way to school, which I don't usually do when I
sleep till my usual time.
messages.3952:
Even more oddly, Tsukishiro greeted me, although she
immediately cut the conversation off from there.
messages.4055:
I also met Suginami and Mako... I see, I should learn to
wake up early more often.

messages.148:
My destination was beyond the school gates, to buy some
stuff.
messages.208: Right at the school gates, I unexpectedly saw Tsukishiro.
messages.270: "Tsukishiro! Are you heading out to do shopping too?"
messages.336: Noticing me, she nodded in answer to my question.
messages.385: "Heh, it's odd to meet you here."
messages.432:
I pointed out the school gates, indirectly suggesting "let's
go together", and started off.
messages.595: The gloves came off once again, and after a few pats;
messages.668:
"Nope, Alice is looking for notebooks for the afternoon
classes."
messages.736: Getting that doll to talk won't solve anything.
messages.798:
As long as Tsukishiro keeps up this stance, she won't ever
get used to talking to people.
messages.866: I want to get her to talk to me, somehow.
messages.911: "Can't you just buy that at the school's stationery shop?"
messages.992:
"The ones Alice uses can't be bought at school. We have no
choice but to go out to get it."
messages.1086: "That's odd. Notebooks all look the same to me."
messages.1273:
Suddenly opening her mouth like that, I could only force out
a vague, stammered reply.
messages.1624: "We thought you'd be kinda different than you are now..."
messages.1743:
"Yeah, like how you were during last year's Christmas and
graduation parties."
messages.1838:
This school has a lot of yearly events that students have to
participate in, such as the Christmas and graduation
parties.
messages.1955:
I ended up being involved in a lot of mischief at those
functions last year.
messages.2017:
Along with Suginami, I was quickly placed on the discplinary
committee's blacklist.
messages.2085:
Well, I guess this year being the one I graduate myself, has
made me mellow down a bit.
messages.2391:
I don't normally partake in gossping, but to hear that even
the lowerclassmen know my name, gives me a sense of pride.
messages.2492: I could practically feel my head getting bigger.
messages.2580:
"Shirakawa-sensei and the other senseis talk about you
often, saying things like "Don't be like Asakura and
Suginami from 3rd year"."
messages.2712: Those people... talking like that about me behind my back...
messages.2768:
Wait till they see the newspapers tomorrow... "Student
refuses to go to school!", how good that'd look.
messages.2881: "You're sure talking a lot today, aren't you?"
messages.2960:
"Me? Mm, but that's because I'm basically a proxy for Alice
trying to communicate her feelings."
messages.3170:
"Well, whatever. I know a good stationery shop at the main
street... I have stuff to do there, shall we go together?"
messages.3401:
Doesn't seem like they dislike the idea, but in the same
vein, I can't really tell whether they enjoy it either.
messages.3506: Well, at least getting this far is good enough.
messages.3733:
While heading out to do some shopping during lunch break, I
ran into Tsukishiro.
messages.3797:
At my attempts to start conversation, Tsukishiro once again
used the doll to answer for her.
messages.3859:
The limit of what I could find out, was that the doll was
"Alice's proxy in trying to communicate her feelings."
messages.3984:
But when I asked her herself, she said she didn't
particularly want to talk.
messages.4052:
Well, I don't understand at all, but it's not something I
can't stand, at least.

messages.210:
"...Hm? Aaaahh, can people here this? Oh well, I'd give it a
try..."
messages.274:
Slightly fearful words emnated from the speakers stationed
at the ceiling.
messages.416: "Onii-chan, can you hear me~? Let's each lunch together~"
messages.520: "I'd be waiting at the broadcasting room, onii-chan♪"
messages.603: I didn't know someone had a sister in this school as well.
messages.663:
"Anyway, I should hurry up. The bread will all be gone by
now..."
messages.835: "Ah~... unya, testing testing... mmm, can you hear me?"
messages.1012: "Do you dislike eating lunch with me that much!?"
messages.1091:
"It took so much effort to get to the broadcasting system to
-- ah, t, teacher? U, unyaaa!"
messages.1248:
Yet, a while after, Koyomi-sensei was angry at me because of
that.
messages.1486:
From the speakers came an enigmatic voice, calling out for
her brother.
messages.1540:
It was actually Sakura, trying to ask me to eat lunch with
her.
messages.1626:
And she somehow managed to get me in trouble with the
teachers as well...

messages.182:
With bought bread in hand, I start to return to the
classroom.
messages.248: A tiny little thing rolled past me on the floor.
messages.350:
Immediately following it was Koyomi-sensei. She had her
glasses on top of her head, holding our her hands like a
zombie.
messages.475: "Damnit... I can't see a thing without my glasses..."
messages.543:
She immediately stopped as I called to her back. As she put
back her glasses, I chased the rolling thing.
messages.656: It was a can of coffee, unsweetened.
messages.749:
She looked around a bit, then put her glasses back on her
face.
messages.836:
I hand over the canned coffee with a little grin, rubbing my
head a bit.
messages.911:
"Sorry, I've been forgetful lately. And I've not really been
able to keep up my appearance either..."
messages.1071:
"I'm not normally one to exert my powers as a civil servant,
but if the time and place is right..."
messages.1199: "Asakura-kun, I hope you go through graduation smoothly."
messages.1275: With the voice of a kitten, I meekly raise the white flag.
messages.1337:
"Glad we have an understanding. ...That's right, what drink
do you want? I should treat you for getting my coffee back."
messages.1472:
"Well, as long as your request involves coffee, it'll be
fine."
messages.1635: "Didn't you invite me here for coffee?"
messages.1689: "Right. What do you think I'm doing here?"
messages.1806: My eyes caught a beaker sitting right next to it.
messages.1862:
...I see。 The beaker's probably used as a container to hold
the coffee.
messages.1940:
Although really, if coffee can be made here, I don't see the
point in buying canned coffee.
messages.2050:
"Hm? Didn't you want to come here to have a drink of
coffee?"
messages.2130:
"Well, yes. But I thought it would be canned coffee from a
vending machine or something."
messages.2217: "It's good to drink normal coffee once in a while."
messages.2275: ...Is she saying this coffee she's brewing isn't...
messages.2360:
I quickly turn to leave, but Koyomi-sensei managed to stop
me before I got to the door.
messages.2425:
"Wait, I'm just joking, sheesh. Just grab a chair and sit
down."
messages.2504:
Still wondering whether my stomach will really be okay, I
take her advice and sit down on a nearby chair.
messages.2592:
I've seen raw food being prepared before, so watching coffee
brew isn't my idea of a good time.
messages.2678: I randomly look around the room.
messages.2738:
"Don't make yourself look so conspicious. I do have a sister
in this school."
messages.2830:
With her back turned to me, she made an idle complaint, with
me being unable to see her expression.
messages.2944:
"Mm? You're calling her so freely already? You two are that
close, huh?"
messages.3014: "No no. She's just, how you say it... very friendly."
messages.3097: That word seemed to get stuck in between her teeth.
messages.3188: "...Are you saying you can see my face through my back?"
messages.3298:
"Myself, of course. Anyway, about Kotori. You don't think
she's friendly?"
messages.3499:
It wasn't a beaker, but a fragrant cup with steam rising
from it that was handed to me.
messages.3578:
"Kotori... she's definitely a socialable person, but she
always seems like she's overdoing it. From what I see,
anyway.
messages.3687:
Koyomi-sensei opened the previously-rolling canned coffee
using the pull-top, and took a drink from it.
messages.3795:
"Well, whether you or anyone else, if she wants to make
friends with them, there's nothing I can say about it."
messages.3887: "Would I be an "anyone else" as well?"
messages.4007:
"I wouldn't consider you just "one of them". You should be
happy for that."
messages.4085:
"Both ways, she's so popular that if she were to marry, I
bet there'd be an unofficial day of mourning for this
island."
messages.4395:
I bumped into Koyomi-sensei, and somehow or other, she ended
up treating me to some coffee.
messages.4459:
From talking about private and public matters, the subject
of her sister came up.
messages.4533:
Apparently, Kotori mixing around so well gives her something
of a bad feeling... I wonder why.

messages.186: Tamaki and Kudou were talking, behind the school gym.
messages.252:
The school's number one pretty boy, and the traditional
beauty Tamaki...
messages.289: They actually look pretty good together.
messages.332:
I wonder what they're talking about? They seem pretty
serious...
messages.453: Kudou noticed me in the shadows.
messages.480: "Hey, you two. Sorry for the rudeness."
messages.529:
I wasn't meaning to eavesdrop, but the circumstances
certainly didn't look good anyway.
messages.593:
I tried to laugh off the tension, as I made myself more
visible to the two of them.
messages.683: "Am I interrupting something? Like a confession, perhaps?"
messages.856: I mockingly rubbed my chin and smirked at Kudou.
messages.916:
"You've got it wrong, Asakura. I was just asking
Konomiya-san about something..."
messages.982:
"Now now, it's not something you need to hide! It's good to
be close, after all!"
messages.1058:
Of course, I knew. Kudou probably guessed that I was just
acting, as well.
messages.1132:
If it really was a confession scene though, I'd be the real
idiot.
messages.1272:
My eyes instinctively moved to the sound of the passionate
voice. The previously silent Tamaki had spoken.
messages.1334:
It took me a second to digest the sudden change in
atmosphere.
messages.1371:
It was rare to see the usually calm Tamaki, so emotional
about somehting.
messages.1569:
Tamaki was still staring at me, the seriousness on her face
plain to see.
messages.1608:
It was an atmosphere that indicated that all jokes had to be
stopped.
messages.1645: "Y, you don't need to react that much..."
messages.1731: "Yeah, you know... it was just a joke."
messages.1803:
He may not have directly acknowledged it, but he certanily
recognized it...
messages.1912: Tamaki was genuinely taken aback at my "revelation".
messages.2000:
"W, why did I... why did I act so strongly... what should
I...?"
messages.2092: Tamaki's words were garbled and rushed.
messages.2172:
"I'm very sorry, for speaking so loudly... to you as well,
Kudou-sama."
messages.2309:
"No, well... I was making a stupid joke as well, so I'm
sorry too."
messages.2415: "Hm, the air's gotten darker... I shall head back to class."
messages.2524: Running away successfully, Tamaki left for the classroom.
messages.2592: "I guess I went a bit too far."
messages.2653: "Perhaps. A young woman's heart is complex."
messages.2880:
During lunch, I went to the back of the gym, and found Kudou
and Tamaki engrossed in a serious conversation.
messages.2952:
I teased them about the relationship, which Tamaki got
seirously angry about.
messages.3014: Did I say something that bad?

messages.141:
The plant that Tsukishiro was taking care of, didn't seem to
show any signs of growth.
messages.203:
It looked like it was weak, but still trying it's best to
live.
messages.275:
Tsukishiro's taking care of it with all she's got, though. I
don't think it'd die just yet.
messages.367: I do wonder what kind of flower this is, though.
messages.406:
Not that I know much about biology, but it seems very
strange for a plant to be growing in this damp, dark place.
messages.540: From behind me, a tiny voice broke the silence.
messages.579:
In this deserted place, there's no mistaking who it belonged
to.
messages.735:
"Nothing, just checking on the plant. For now, it seems to
be growing, doesn't it?"
messages.819:
I was lying through my teeth, of course; this plant didn't
seem like it was enjoying life at all.
messages.940: Tsukishiro stopped beside me, and squatted down.
messages.975:
Her gaze never left the plant as she whispered things to it,
and would nod to it from time to time.
messages.1076:
"Well, I don't know much, but it seems to be an important
plant..."
messages.1182:
"I'm heading back now... what about you? Want to go
together?"
messages.1250: Tsukishiro glanced at my face from the side.
messages.1334: And with that, returned to her vegetation-staring.
messages.1377:
Like a geriatric, I took a deep breath before I got to my
feet.

plenty of time to spare.
messages.2038: "Alright, Tsukishiro! Let's head to school together."
messages.2109: We started walking down the Sakura Avenue, side-by-side.
messages.2191: "Huh, nii-san? How did you get here so..."
messages.2242:
"Yo, Nemu. --Unlike most days, today, I am the princess's
escort!"
messages.2383: Tsukishiro started tugging on my shirt.
messages.2420:
I tunred to face her, and noticed her face had gotten red,
while the sleeve-tugging didn't stop.
messages.2544: Following Tsukishiro's tugging, I headed into the school.
messages.2769:
As Nemu had gone off earlier, I left the house by myself,
and was spotted by the driving Seiba.
messages.2859:
It was to shorten the route to school, apparently. But,
hearing that it was a request from Tsukishiro herself, made
me happy.
messages.2964:
Dropped off at the start of Sakura Avenue, and feeling like
a princess's escort, Tsukishiro and I headed to school
together.

messages.199:
The morning of the day of exams is always an interesting
sight.
messages.261:
Students everywhere were holding a textbook in one hand,
with black rings around their eyes.
messages.331:
Those who weren't, were simply smiling brightly, having
obviously given up.
messages.393: I guess I would fall in the latter category...
messages.528: Kudou appeared from within the crowd of students.
messages.765:
With a smile as radiant as the blue sky, another student
made his appearance.
messages.943: ...Ever thought it had something to do with you?
messages.990:
Not able to hear the words from my mind, Suginami continued
with his wry grin.
messages.1082:
"Haha, worried about the test? Don't bother, there's nothing
you can do till the paper's in front of you!"
messages.1183: "Thinking negatively now will only make it worse later."
messages.1241:
That is pretty logical advice... But of course, it's coming
from someone who shouldn't have any worries about it
messages.1401: Oh well, no point in being resentful.
messages.1436:
After all, I'd find out the true extent of my capabilities
from here on...
messages.1681:
On the day of the tests, I was talking to Kudou in a
half-defeated state, when Suginami came by.
messages.1759: His easy demeanour really shows how unfair this world is.
messages.1831: ...Well, I'd just have to do my best anyway.

messages.226:
After breaking through what seemed like a tunnel of sakura
petals, I finally could look at the blue sky above.
messages.300:
"This kind of day would be perfect for just lazing around at
home..."
messages.376:
Forgetting about breakfast, lying in bed and slowly dozing
off...
messages.506: "I don't think that has anything to do with good weather..."
messages.570: A meek voice from behind caused me to turn my head.
messages.609: Kotori had a sheepish smile on her face.
messages.753: "How are you feeling for today's test? Uneasy?"
messages.802:
"Ahh. I'm not exactly proud to say this, but I'm always
sleeping during lessons. And the exam scope is pretty vague
as well."
messages.955: "That's really something not to be proud of..."
messages.1025: "Well, no reason to just stand here and talk. Let's go."
messages.1207: "You don't need to do last-minute cramming, right?"
messages.1254:
Kotori's not just a pretty face, she has a good head as
well.
messages.1381: Kotori stroked her chin with her index finger and nodded.
messages.1433:
"I do look over the points I take down during lessons the
night before an exam. Besides, the teacher did say the exam
scope."
messages.1552: "Then you know roughly what will come out on the exam?"
messages.1659: Maybe I could make use of this.
messages.1690:
There may not be that much time till the exam, but I don't
have to go in knowing absolutely nothing.
messages.1774: If I do this, I might not be in as much trouble as I think!
messages.1898: Kotori gave me an innocent smile.
messages.2157:
I can barely concentrate now, I won't be able to cram much
more in...
messages.2215:
And there's no real point in putting up a hopeless struggle
now.
messages.2281:
Besides, I don't really want to disgrace myself any further
in front of her, already appearing before with these
bloodshot eyes.
messages.2522: "I said do your best for the exams."
messages.2594:
I'd have to count on the powers of my luck to pull me
through.
messages.2660:
As I decide that, Kotori for some reason started smiling
happily.
messages.2897:
It's now the first day of tests. Kotori caught me in the
midsts of one of my traversals into an alternate reality.
messages.2971:
With her academic excellence and her basic understanding of
the exam scope, I thought of trying to finagle it out of
her, but eventually thought better of it.
messages.3061: I'd rely on my own power for it.

messages.202: I entered the classroom, trying to stifle my yawn.
messages.241:
Cry or scream however much I want, today's the day of the
exams.
messages.346:
Even though it seems like I haven't prepared for the exams,
the true effectiveness of my sleepstudying will be shown
now.
messages.495:
A voice as refreshing as the morning breeze floated to my
ears.
messages.561: I turned around to find Tamaki, a gentle smile on her face.
messages.667: "It's the day of the exams. I can't be late."
messages.729: "...Although it might be for the best, if I was."
messages.833:
"You can choose to take the supplementary exam instead if
you have a good reason to be late."
messages.966: "It sounds like you had trouble picking which to do."
messages.1045: I replied her vague insinuation with vagueness myself.
messages.1194:
"You might say so... you sound awfully confident, don't
you."
messages.1315:
She tilted her head to the side in puzzlement. These
innocent ones are always the ones who know the best ways.
messages.1467:
"How do you study for the exams? You have some secret
method, don't you?"
messages.1611: "I just memorize the contents of the textbook."
messages.1673: My voice came out sounding incredibly stupid.
messages.1714: "H... hold up. You completely... memorize... everything?"
messages.1823: She gave me a big smile.
messages.1848:
Ugh, that kind of smile at this time of the day will
brighten my mood!
messages.1889:
I guess that's the one surefire way of doing well for
tests...
messages.2014:
Tamaki smiled again, treating it as if it's the most normal
thing in the world to do.
messages.2134:
"It is quite similar to the memorization of the Shinto
ritual prayers."
messages.2291: They aren't God's messengers for nothing!
messages.2396: "Alright, then I'd test you a little."
messages.2452:
Not that I don't believe her, but the way she pronounces
such a thing with such confidence... I have to confirm it.
messages.2547:
I took several textbooks from under my desk and plopped them
on top, flipping to a suitable page.
messages.2703: A bit of tension crept into her face.
messages.2744:
"The high priest of the Tendai sect, Ennin, opened a temple
in the far northeast of Japan. What was the temple called?"
messages.3008:
Just like the TV show, I paused shortly before delivering
the verdict.
messages.3081:
Long enough for me to see the sheer confidence that she
possessed.
messages.3217: Tamaki patted her chest in relief.
messages.3269:
"There's every chance that you could've just remembered this
question, eh?"
messages.3342: "If you think so, please move on to the next question."
messages.3385:
With the confidence back in her after her correct answer,
her previous trembling had vanished.
messages.3453:
Instead, her cheeks were slightly flushed from the
excitement, with those limpid eyes staring straight at me...
messages.3590: All I could do was to stare back at them.
messages.3670: Tamaki become puzzled, peering closer into my face.
messages.3840:
The closer she got, the more of her sweet scent I could
smell, which drove my heart even faster.
messages.3918:
I quickly distracted myself by returning my gaze to the
textbook.
messages.4035:
"Who is the author of the book "Futon", and what genre is
it?"
messages.4119:
"The author is Tayama Katai, and it is under the naturalism
genre."
messages.4259:
"It is an art style orginating from France. It focuses on
sudden impressions from the brain to create pieces of art."
messages.4440:
Every question I threw at her, was answered impeccably. She
seemed really happy at her work.
messages.4528:
It was the first time I'd seen her smile so brightly,
unrestrained.
messages.4596: "Hmm, you really did memorize everything. That's amazing."
messages.4680:
"It isn't really... if you can memorize the general points,
it's easier to remember everything."
messages.4760: Tamaki abashedly smiled in her reply.
messages.4797:
"Doing that still pretty much confirms a good score. It's
amazing."
messages.4875:
"I couldn't possibly indiscriminately memorize everything
like that."
messages.4926:
The fact that she can memorize all those ritual prayers is
already several steps above me.
messages.5021:
"That's not true. The more times you read the textbook, the
easier it is to remember what you read."
messages.5135: "Even the sound of the pages being flipped."
messages.5193:
If I had such a brilliant memory that could recall the sound
of pages being flipped, I wouldn't be worrying now.
messages.5318: "I was thinking of memorizing "First Love" that way, now..."
messages.5378: "Huh, "First Love"? That poem mentioned in the textbook?"
messages.5451:
That reminded me, it was said that there'd be a question
where you'd have to recite an entire verse from a poem...
messages.5615: She paused for a little, and spoke after some thought.
messages.5699: "...Would you like to memorize it with me?"
messages.5806:
"Ahhh, with the Goddess of Recollection guiding me, I might
just be able to..."
messages.5940: Her words were tinged with joy.
messages.6229:
"(No matter how many times I hear it, I can't get over the
comfort I feel from her voice...)"
messages.6326:
People generally look to Miko for assurance, guidance, and a
sense of safety...
messages.6382: Is that the trait that Tamaki possesses, as well?
messages.6425: Her behaviour may be strange at times...
messages.6456: But it adds to her cuteness as well.
messages.6508:
Man. Thinking so much while reciting, I'm not remembering
anything at all.
messages.6608: "Meek as a lamb, I ask of you."
messages.6647: "Something as a something, I ask of something."
messages.6713: Sorry for having a crappy memory.
messages.6784:
"...Asakura-sama, when did you encounter your first feelings
of love?"
messages.6848: Tamaki threw that question at me from nowhere.
messages.6995:
When I was small, I used to think everything I felt for
girls was love... but now, I feel it's more like an
extension of friendship.
messages.7126:
It's different from really having someone you love, someone
you can't stop thinking of, someone always in your heart.
messages.7272:
"The feelings you get from your first love will surely
remain strong even as years pass..."
messages.7383:
Honestly, I've never truly experienced it, so I couldn't say
much.
messages.7428: Yet, my heart seemed to tell me that her words rang true.
messages.7579: But as she said that, she shook her head rapidly.
messages.7659: "However, first love is never true anyway..."
messages.7702: She spoke slowly, pronouncing every syllable.
messages.7776: Her eyes gazed deeply into mine.
messages.7824: Those serious eyes made me self-conscious.
messages.7863: I felt like she was seeing through my feelings.
messages.7912: Tamaki opened her lips once... then closed it immediately.
messages.8008: Her mouth shut firmly tight, again.
messages.8039: Tamaki... what's that girl trying to say?
messages.8124:
Maybe she's talking about that supposed "deep bond" we
have...
messages.8180:
She may know as much as me about it, but it's still a
promise of some sort when we were younger...
messages.8242:
I don't know what she's trying to convey, but I felt like I
couldn't let her continue.
messages.8316:
"I think your first love would be just as true a love as any
other."
messages.8378:
Despite knowing nothing about it, I just tried to say what I
thought.
messages.8455:
When Tamaki heard my words, whatever she was feeling, a tiny
smile crept onto her lips.
messages.8732:
I found Tamaki in the classroom on the day of the first
exams. She seemed composed and confident of them.
messages.8798:
I tried to uncover her secret studying methods, but
apparently, she simply memorizes the entire textbook.
messages.8868:
We tried to memorize Shimazaki Touson's "First Love"
together, and she tried to ask me something.
messages.8960:
But she decided against it. Wonder what she was trying to
say...?

messages.161:
On the way to checking on Alice's plant, I bumped into the
aforementioned there.
messages.356:
She held an empty water can in her hands. In front of her,
the plant had drops of water still residuant, sparkling.
messages.465: "There goes my reason for being here then..."
messages.514:
I started to scratch my head. Now what should I do... I
don't really want to just leave like this.
messages.604:
Partly because of the plant, but more importantly, because
of Tsukishiro herself.

messages.721: Her hair shook along with her head, no.
messages.756:
"I haven't either. Want to eat lunch at the cafeteria
together?"
messages.826:
Tsukishiro, thinking hard about it, tilted her head left and
right alternately, until eventually,
messages.979: Little by little, she was starting to open up.

I ordered the curry pork, and my unexpected lunch companion
ordered the curry rice.
messages.1259: We found a table, and started digging in.
messages.1302:
Her doll and gloves were both placed on the seat next to
her.
messages.1366:
It seems like the gloves help her carry the doll... or
something.

Tsukishiro still wasn't used to talking idly, so her

messages.1503: But, that she's even trying, is a blessing.

messages.1661:
Seeing that tiny mouth nibble on the curry rice was just

messages.1737: The nearly untouched rice portion reminded me of something.
messages.1865:
Tsukishiro looked at me suspiciously. After some thought,
and with a slight blush,
messages.2019:
"I bet you turn it upside down before you start eating,

messages.2151: The embarassment on her face was clear now.
messages.2250: "Next time, let's make those soap bubbles together~"
messages.2316:
Tsukishiro, thinking about something, tilted her head left
and right again.
messages.2463:
"There's some safety functions and stuff that prevent that
from happening nowadays."
messages.2567:
Just like before, she hung her head low, her cheeks flushed
with redness.
messages.2659:
"Ahhh, it's Asakura-senpai and Tsukishiro-san! Are you
eating lunch together?"
messages.2780: Miharu was sitting down at the table right next to ours.
messages.2920: "Hehe, everyone's eating curry, it must taste good today!"
messages.2982: Miharu giggled at her own sentence.
messages.3009:
Looking closely, it isn't just Miharu, but her two friends
as well, who had ordered something curry-related.
messages.3111: "It's like we're living in India right now!"
messages.3160:
This is Japanese curry anyway... which made me notice
something weird about hers.
messages.3224: "...What's that you're eating with the curry?"
messages.3340: "Ba, banana curry... you must have a stomach of steel..."
messages.3412:
The girls sitting across from Miharu, hearing me say what
they didn't have the heart to, nodded their agreement.
messages.3528:
"Well excuse me! Banana curry is an exquisite dish! The
spiciness of curry mixed with the sweetness of banana..."
messages.3670: Her eyes started sparkling. Her and her banana fetish...
messages.3883:
With tension in the air, Tsukishiro answered the
stll-high-strung Miharu.
messages.3947: Miharu's ears suddenly perked up like a puppy dog.
messages.4033:
"Tsukishiro-san, can I ask a question...? That curry, is it
the sweet type?"
messages.4208: "I knew it! I knew it had to be!"
messages.4253:
Her innocently cheerful smile was enough to chase away the
tension.
messages.4327: Speaking again, with much more joy in her words,
messages.4390: "Hey, hey, can I ask another question?"
messages.4458: Tsukishiro, half-frightened, couldn't do much besides nod.
messages.4556:
At that moment, I was convinced that Miharu and I had the

messages.4804:
Tsukishiro and I ended up eating lunch together. We both

messages.4925:
Seeing that tiny mouth nibble on the curry rice was just
adorable.
messages.5013:
Of course, it was sweet. And she turned her pudding upside

would occasionally swallow them.

Koyomi quietly took the attendance as the rest of the class
had their heads buried in their textbooks.

The first day of the exams has finally come. Everyone came
to school on time today, and using their last bits of time
studying for all they were worth.
messages.677:
Then again, Nemu had had her head up and waiting. Suginami
as well.

At the teacher's approval, all the students started moving

their pencils.

I take a copy of the test paper and flip it around, looking

With the sound of pencils being sharpened all around me, I

And despite having this many before lunch, there's even more
coming in the afternoon...
messages.314: Well, nothing'd be done by just standing around sighing.
messages.366: I should just decide where to go for lunch!
messages.604:
The morning exams of the first day were over. Still this

messages.707: Oh well, time for lunch, lunch. --And a bit more studying.

messages.147: "(I need a breath of fresh air...)"
messages.194: 4 exams in a row take a lot out of you.
messages.293:
I opened the steel door to the rooftop, and the wind raced
to greet me. The feeling of the wind on my face was great.
messages.369: I stretched my arms out, fully enjoying the great weather.
messages.437:
Behind me, the door made a loud slam as it shut itself
tight.
messages.509: I turned to face the owner of the voice--
messages.604:
It was Koyomi-sensei, leaning on a fence. A cigarette hung
from her lips, with white clouds of smoke emerging from it.
messages.744: "What you see, is what you get..."

"Invigiliating exams is as boring as it gets. Even us

With her cigarette stick exhausted, she rubbed the remains

Once again, she breathed out, filling the air in front of

messages.1557: "(The hell have you been inhaling before, then!?)"
messages.1621: A chill ran down my spine.
messages.1656: This teacher is a real enigma.
messages.1832: At the rooftop, I found Koyomi-sensei having a smoke.
messages.1875: I thought tabacco is supposed to be bad for your health...

Thanks to the call of nature, the noontime battle for bread
is almost certainly lost by now.

"If I went now, everything edible would be sold out
already."
messages.310: "I guess I'd eat at the cafeteria... hm, isn't that Kotori?

I bet she doesn't even notice how dangerous it is to do that

"Then why are you carrying so much food at a time? Is

Although Kotori's really popular among the boys, she's has

As if telling me a secret, her face started getting closer

I surveyed the surroundings around me, calmly chewing on my

Ina way, this was completely like me, and in another way,

The things I didn't care about, I completely shoved to the

My words at least manage to wake her out of her trance, and

"Alright, let's go! I'd treat you to a chocolate banana on
the way."

This evening, thinking that Tsukishiro would be behind the
gym as usual, I went there to check on her.
messages.3286:
But she wasn't present, and a feeling of uneasiness crept
onto me.
messages.3358:
On the way back, I met the girl herself, heading back
through the park from shopping. Apparently, she had already
went to see the plant earlier.
messages.3452:
Fully expecting rejection, I asked her to head back
together.
messages.3514: Instead, she nodded with a faint smile.

messages.207: I've suddenly started sneezing. The pollen, maybe?
messages.277:
When walking, the spring temperature is just right, but just
sitting and not moving around left me scrambling for warmth.
messages.531:
I lifted my head as I my nose sniffed unconciously, to the
sight of Kotori handing me a tissue.
messages.619: And next to her was Kudou, ever-smiling.
messages.774: Grinning, Kotori passed me a few pocket tissues.
messages.954: "I didn't know sakura pollen was pink in colour."
messages.1048: "That's... like looking for treasure, isn't it?
messages.1119:
I rolled up the tissue in a ball and threw it in a nearby
trash bin.
messages.1237:
"Nothing much. It's spring after all, when being outdoors
feels great."
messages.1303: "What about you two? What are you doing?"
messages.1401:
"Same as you. The weather was good, so we went out to enjoy
it."
messages.1470: "And we just happened to bump into each other."
messages.1595: She says that them meeting me was a complete coincidence.
messages.1730:
With a finger on her lips, Kotori stared into my eyes for
awhile, then suddenly pulled back and smiled.
messages.1819: "Well, if you're not being skeptic, then it's fine."
messages.1885: The only thing that Kotori gave was a mysterious smile.
messages.1926:
"In any case, it's amazing, everyone with nothing to do in
this feel-good Sunday under the blue sky..."
messages.2068: "...I did say we were taking a walk."
messages.2107: "Well, is that really something to do?"
messages.2268: "Heyy, it's not a battle or anything."
messages.2352:
"...Anyway, want to just take a walk? No point just standing
around here talking."
messages.2486: The three of us started walking together.
messages.2547:
The sweet scent of sakura petals could be smelled, as a
sudden gust of wind blew them past us, and through Kotori's
hair.
messages.2613:
Kotori controlled her hair with her fingers, all the while
wearing a carefree grin.
messages.2744:
I look towards Kotori and gave her a sly grin while nodding
my head.
messages.2798:
"Better be more careful of the wind's effect on your skirt
rather than on your hair."
messages.2860:
Kotori, for some reason, started scowling at Kudou on my
remark.
messages.3167: Compared to walking about alone, it was far more enjoyable.

messages.141:
Lotering around the shopping district earlier, I had bumped
into Tamaki.
messages.219:
I ended up helping her on her shopping, and carrying her
bags. We were heading back to the shrine.
messages.311:
After we finished climbing up the entire flight of stairs,
Tamaki bowed courteously to me.
messages.463:
"Not only for accompanying me while shopping, but for
carrying all the bags as well..."
messages.547:
"You'd help me out if I needed it, too. Don't worry about
it."
messages.607: I managed to get that out in between deep breaths of air.
messages.641:
Holding all these bags, and walking up that many steps to
the shrine, is no mean feat.
messages.703:
Taking one final deep breath, I spied a group of small
kimono-clad girls from the corner of my eye.
messages.837:
A bunch of adults near them were taking pictures of the Miko
litter. Seems like they're the parents of the bunch.
messages.897:
The girls were in high spirits, constantly fussed over by
their parents.
messages.974:
I sneaked a peek beside me; Tamaki was watching the girls as
well.
messages.1026: I kept my gaze on the girl beside me.
messages.1047: I wonder what kind of kid she was when she was young...
messages.1090: Thoughts like that flitted past my head.
messages.1152: "Ah yes, today is the Girl's Festival."
messages.1282:
The little doll hanging by the side of the front gate
should've clued me in...
messages.1366:
"I'd spent more time shopping than I expected... I will have
to hurry to ready the preprations."
messages.1501: "...So, for today, you're a stage hand?"
messages.1587: "Yes, the main attraction for today, are these children."
messages.1680: I suppose age isn't a factor at all during festivals.
messages.1734:
Even kids can offer their blessings for the Girl's Festival
too...
messages.1790: I can do a little something for her, at least.
messages.1945:
With the confusion clear on her face and tilted head, she
held out both her hands to me.
messages.2021:
With the image of the gaggle of little animals fresh in my
head, I visualized a pink-coloured figure.
messages.2111: "(...My feelings may not change the taste, but...)"
messages.2160:
I put all my emotions into making it as delicious as
possible.
messages.2201: I then placed my hand over Tamaki's outstretched hands,
messages.2390:
"I kinda tore up the wrapping already, but... here's my gift
for the festival. Work hard, Tamaki."
messages.2630: Seeing her this happy made me feel happy as well.
messages.2705: "But, when did you find the time to buy this?"
messages.2769: ...I can't exactly tell her that I just created it.
messages.2829: "Don't worry about that, just enjoy it."
messages.2927:
With a smile enveloping her entire face, she brought the
manjuu to her open mouth.
messages.2974:
The taste of the manjuu seemed to brighten her smile even
further.
messages.3019:
The usually cool, calm and collected Tamaki was now looking
very childishly happy.
messages.3091:
I didn't know how to take the sudden change in her
demeanour.
messages.3188:
The way she normally was, it couldn't have been an
exaggeration, but...
messages.3310: She silently nodded, while still staring at me.
messages.3387:
"Asakura-sama's sweets appear to have a strange power. I
always feel energetic after eating one."
messages.3503:
"W, well, I did work hard in ma... ah, ahem, I'm glad the
end result was good."
messages.3585:
At my nervous reason, Tamaki's smile grew even more
brilliant.
messages.3654:
"Asakura-sama's thoughts... feelings... and kindness... I
can feel all of them in this wagashi."
messages.3784:
Even though I made it to make her happy, her praise still
embarassed me...
messages.3909:
"Thank you for the meal. I must prepare the sake now,
though..."
messages.4021:
Thanking me once again, she walked into the shrine with her
bags.
messages.4122: I started on the road home.
messages.4317:
On the way back to the shrine from helping Tamaki with
shopping, we found a gaggle of little girls, it being the
Girl's Festival.
messages.4426:
I made a wagashi for Tamaki as a present, which made her
overjoyed.

messages.139:
"Hoo... I sure moved around a lot today. But it was the end
of exams, after all."
messages.310:
While I was arranging my bed to sleep in, Nemu opened the
door from the hallway.
messages.409: A secret visit at night, maybe?
messages.475:
"Tomorrow, I have to leave early for disciplinary commiittee
work. Can you wake up yourself in the morning?"
messages.553: Nemu worriedly posed her question to me.
messages.594: "You don't have to worry, I'm not a kid anymore."
messages.698: She answered that way, but her face told otherwise.
messages.758:
"Don't work yourself too hard either. You'd be manning the
school gate, right?"
messages.818:
The weather now is still cold, especially in the morning.
Standing there for hours just for "work" would be torture.
messages.945:
"Sorry for worrying you, but there has to be someone to
catch all the latecomers."
messages.1040:
That wasn't quite what I meant... oh well, it'd work out in
the end.
messages.1209: Nemu left my room, her bell leaving a ringing noise echoing.
messages.1254:
"(If I meet her at the school gates late, her reaction would
be...)"
messages.1316:
I had better not sleep in tomorrow; I set my alarm clock to
make sure.
messages.1463: After setting the alarm, I continued studying.
messages.1521: After setting the alarm, I continued studying.
messages.1570: After setting the alarm, I slept.
messages.1743:
Nemu had disciplinary committee work tomorrow. She was fine
with being alone, and not worried at all.
messages.1840:
She was more worried about me being late for school. The
morning temperature is still cold, and the work would
involve her standing at the school gate for awhile...
messages.1959:
Anyway, I'd better not let her see me coming in late
tomorrow.

messages.162:
Really, that sister of mine... she'd rather burn that ask
someone for help.
messages.235: I wrapped myself up into my futon.
messages.270: In any case, I better not sleep late tomorrow.
messages.330: There may not be anyone to pick up my remains after...
messages.621:
To make sure that I wouldn't sleep late, I set my alarm
clock, then hurried off to sleep.

Koyomi-sensei was holding the class register, staring down

messages.536:
"Class is still on. If you want to sleep, wait a few more

Holding the register in one hand, Koyomi-sensei returned to
her desk.
messages.656:
If I yawn while the weekly duty is doing his stuff, she'd

messages.201: A calm voice floated around my ears.
messages.265: "C'mon, it's time to get up already~"
messages.304: It felt like a transparent-sounding voice.
messages.367: "Geez... you're really not gonna get up?"

messages.469:
The atmosphere suddenly shifted, and I could feel Kotori

messages.531: "If you don't get up, I'm going to kiss you."
messages.572:
I could feel her breath tickling my ears as she whispered

messages.647: Having heard that, there's no way I'm going to get up now.
messages.715: "(Of course I wouldn't, I'm a guy after all!)"
messages.744:
Waiting for the feeling of Kotori's soft touch, I
concentrated all my sensitivity on my cheek.
messages.826: "(Then again, it could be on the lips...)"
messages.1026: And the darkness around me suddenly subsided--
messages.1180: A voice I wasn't expecting rang out.

As I opened my eyes, the figure of Koyomi-sensei filled my

messages.1384: "The lesson will be over soon, stay awake until then."
messages.1433: With that, she went back to the front of the classroom.
messages.1487: "(Don't tell me that was... the attendance record I felt?)"
messages.1612: With nothing else to announce, the class ended.
messages.1737: But at least I managed to sleep till noontime.
messages.1784: Guess it's time to get ready for lunch...
messages.2001: She was gently waking me up...

At Koyomi's signal, Tahata gave the order for the class to

messages.398:
Even I was getting a bit caught up in the sentimentality of

messages.445:
"(It'd probably be worse if I actually had to change
schools...)"
messages.517:
As long as I can't leave this island, I'd surely come back
to here again.
messages.568:
"Well, that's something for the future. Now, to think about
today."
messages.619: As I prepare to go home, I think about what to do.

At Tahata's order, HR ended. Starting from this weekend
would be the graduation party preparation period, then after
that the graduation itself.
messages.907: Anyway, putting that aside, what should I do today.

messages.210: I had a good long stretch.
messages.237: I took a big breath of morning air.
messages.274: This is the best time of the day.
messages.305: But not even the stretch could shake off my sleepiness.
messages.354: Did I anger Morpheus or something?
messages.399:
Maybe I should try and get Tamaki to exorcise him out of
me...
messages.514: Tamaki called out to me, excellent timing.
messages.601: "Oh my, are you still feeling sleepy?"
messages.714:
"I just stayed up last night to watch a late-night TV
program..."
messages.815: "What kind of program would that be?"
messages.844:
"It was a documentary about the Pentagon. They were talking
about how they extracted the truth from people who they
interrogated."
messages.954:
"Heh, that would be the first time I've heard of such a TV
program..."
messages.1052:
"Quite. They show all the weird stuff during the graveyard
period."
messages.1146: "Well, I shall make a note to watch it next time, then."
messages.1183:
"Nah, I don't think girls should be watching such a
program."
messages.1327:
I don't think it's the kind of program that girls would look
very highly upon.
messages.1411:
"I do have an interest in it, as it seemed to have piqued
yours."
messages.1471: "I would like to view the same things you do."
messages.1575: "What kind of TV programs do you like?"
messages.1625:
"Oh, that's right... I've never really watched television
before."
messages.1738: "Don't you have a TV at your home?"
messages.1771: That hits a little close to home...
messages.1817:
"No, I do. We do pay the bills to maintain the television
and radio as well."
messages.1912: "But then, why don't you watch TV?"
messages.1954:
"I am often so busy with my duties that I do not have time
to watch, that's all..."
messages.2031:
"I go to sleep early at night as well... usually, I am
content to watch the news on the television."
messages.2150: "What kind of news has been in vogue recently?"
messages.2225: "Ha ha ha, in vogue... news is not quite a type of fashion."
messages.2333: "I cannot say I agree with you there, then."
messages.2390:
"The most recent story I saw was about a dolphin that
somehow got lost and ended up in a river."
messages.2471:
"I was watching a rescue team try to drag the dolphin up
using a fish hook in order to transport it back to the sea."
messages.2618: "Yes. They do possess have a mysterious power."
messages.2729:
"It is said that when God descends down to this world, he
takes the form of an animal to observe the surroundings."
messages.2834:
Tamaki certainly doesn't seem like the type to be too
interested in politics or economics, with her religious
background.
messages.2899:
"But generally, I prefer reading books over watching
television."
messages.3059: Tamaki seemed slightly uncertain on how to answer.
messages.3286: That gag flew right over her head.
messages.3315:
Now I can really believe her when she says that she doesn't
really watch TV at all.
messages.3375: "Sorry, just pretend I didn't say anything."
messages.3475:
"That was the book written in the Heian Period, by Sei
Shonagon."
messages.3548: "Not quite. It was Murasaki Shikibu who wrote it."
messages.3581: "...Right, right. I knew it was wrong once I said it."
messages.3648: "Ha ha ha, you're really quite amusing..."
messages.3679: Tamaki was politely covering her mouth during her giggles.
messages.3740:
It's not surprising for me to be so slow-witted at this time
of the day though...
messages.3844: "Not really. It's a fabulous romance novel."
messages.3910:
When that was said, the first thing that comes to my mind is
a main character with several girls madly in love with him.
messages.3985: Strange for that to pop up now...
messages.4128:
As I had to study it for Literature before, I read the manga
for the overall story, to study for it.
messages.4224: "I see. I prefer reading the original text."
messages.4296:
That kind of reasoning is completely alien to me... I
couldn't understand the original even if I tried.
messages.4391:
That she can understand that old literature, made my
admiration for her grow even more.
messages.4483:
Tamaki bowed her head slightly, blushing red in
embarassment.
messages.4548:
"All the women in Genji Monogatari neve ever stray from
Genji's side..."
messages.4643: "Everyone always wants to be beside the one they love."
messages.4798:
"Yes. Women, even if the one they love does not love them
back, would rather be beside that person and harbour
unrequited love..."
messages.4933: "That would be a typical girl's feelings, no?"
messages.4984: "I'm a man, I wouldn't ever know."
messages.5049: "Are men typically loved by lots of women?"
messages.5121: "We-ll, I think that depends on the person..."
messages.5206: "I'm not so attractive as to know first-hand."
messages.5247:
The only people I can think of, are those who love me more
like a brother than anything else...
messages.5309: I've never whole-heartedly loved a person either.
messages.5395:
"For myself, I would like to be by the side of the person I
love forever."
messages.5453: I quickly turn my head towards Tamaki.
messages.5501:
For a second, I thought that comment was directed towards
me,
messages.5546: despite all evidence to the contrary.
messages.5573:
And the very fact that Tamaki said such an outburst was
surprising in itself.
messages.5649: So I guess my senses reacted as well.
messages.5745: Tamaki spoke at me, smiling radiantly.
messages.5846: I kept thinking of what Tamaki said.
messages.5887: What am I thinking of, seriously...
messages.6091:
In the morning, as I walked to school in a half-slumbering
state, I met Tamaki.
messages.6173:
After confessing that I stayed up late to watch TV, and
asking her what kind of TV programs she liked, she replied
that she prefered books instead.
messages.6257:
"Genji Monogatari" especially, which she was reading the
original text of at the moment. She then extrapolated on how
it's natural for a woman to, despite having no links to the
man she loves, stay by his side forever.
messages.6358: I wonder what she meant by that.

messages.188: "It's odd for you to invite me out of school for lunch."
messages.250:
"I guess. Recently, I saw an interesting-looking set-lunch
advertised, and thought I'd introduce it around."
messages.338:
From time to time, I'd head out of campus to eat. The school
doesn't prohibit it, so lots of students spend their lunch
break outside.
messages.540:
"I did, but he muttered something like "Today's winds are a
bad omen", and declined."
messages.694: Kudou pushed his hair up with his palm, laughing a little.
messages.805:
"Well, if we don't get moving now, we won't have enough
time."
messages.892: Walking together, we strolled down the Sakura Avenue.
messages.975: That figure in front of us, isn't that Tsukishiro?

Tsukishiro, who had been walking in our direction, reached

messages.1213: "Oy oy, now that's the pot calling the kettle black..."

messages.1525:
Tsukishiro nodded, and opened the vinyl bag she was carrying
to let me look.
messages.1638: Another nod, as she zipped the bag back up.
messages.1715: Tsukishiro's gaze turned to me, worry on her face.
messages.1752: "Ahh, it's nothing, don't worry about it."
messages.1785:
As I answered, she let out a held breath, the relief obvious
on her face.
messages.1864: "A secret that's important to this girl, I suppose."
messages.1945: "If that's the case, then... I won't delve any further."
messages.2053:
As she spoke, she nodded again, then walked at her usual

"So basically, she was late because she had to protect

"Too bad your reasons for tardiness aren't as glorious as

Just then, a lone girl was walking towards us, tottering

The way she was sleepwalking, she was on a collision course

messages.2585: And of course, she was playing with that toy.

Moe-senpai eventually collided with a wall, and fell to the

I went out of campus with Kudou to eat lunch, and we bumped

school.
messages.3384:
Apparently she was late because she went to buy fertilize

messages.3503:
After which, we found Moe-senpai peacefully sleeping next to

messages.166:
"There's just 3 more days to the end of lessons, so keep

party."

With the weekly cleanup duty echoing throughout the room, HR

messages.372:
I didn't have that many memories of the school life here...
but I'd have another three years to make more anyway.
messages.458: "(Well, I'd just enjoy the break while I can.)"
messages.493:
I just wish today's lessons would go faster... I lay my hand
lazily on my desk, as I ready my textbook.
messages.733:
Only three days of lessons left, including today. The
remainder of the school year would be spent on preparations
for the graduation party, and waiting for the graduation
itself.
messages.819:
Really though... besides seeing all the girls in a new
school uniform, I don't have any strong feelings towards

Today's history lesson was even more boring than usual; the
lesson just sounded like an endless robotic drone to me.
messages.193:
It's not that Nakane-sensei's classes are boring... but
she's pretty old, and shows it when she constantly goes off
the topic...
messages.302:
"In times of desperate need, don't forget that grass is
edible."
messages.378: "SUch as the weeds shown here, called..."
messages.425:
With that, she explained the name of the weed, and the
locations it's normally found in.
messages.495:
But why on earth are we learning cooking and survival
techniques now...

messages.311:
All around me, I could hear a cheerful voice, wrapped around
my body, giving me a sense of security.
messages.391:
It's like being in the middle of a dream... but it's not a
dream... The darkness slowly spreaded further...
messages.1051:
My brain fell into a haze, and little by little, I felt like
I was travelling to some place far in the distance...

messages.154: I'd finally arrived at the rooftop to have lunch, but...

Even though the familiar prettily-dressed table was there,

I'd finally decided to go to the rooftop to eat with the
Mizukoshi sisters, but they weren't around.
messages.654: Geez, tell others if you're not going to be there!
messages.689: My stomach continued grumbling in hunger.

messages.210: Did I stay up that late last night? I slept pretty well...

For today, I will rest. The chances of dying from sleep
deprivation are higher than that of dying from hunger.
messages.433: My stomach, just hold on till nighttime, won't you?
messages.673:
Although my stomach was grumbling, there are times where
sleep takes precedence.
messages.745: That was the feeling I had today.

"I want to enjoy a lovingly-made lunchbox once in a
while..."
messages.211:
Staring hard at the bread in my hands, which I had bought
earlier, I mumbled to myself.
messages.271:
Compared to the pains one can go to make a lunchbox, the
actual contents of it don't matter as much.
messages.380:
"But in this case, taste and nutrition would take priority.
If I can't enjoy the love in food, I could enjoy the food
itself..."
messages.512:
Kotori, with a relenting smile, let me have a spoonful of
her lunchbox.
messages.599: I asked her while chewing it.
messages.738: I pretended to shed a few tears of joy.
messages.821: "I wish I could eat this kind of thing every day."
messages.860:
With a sigh, I open my packets of bread. I couldn't get any
of the good ones today...
messages.1015:
"...Under the beautiful stars of the night sky, that would
sound far more appropriate."
messages.1116:
"Does that mean you're trying to escort me to the
guillotine?"
messages.1214:
"Marie Antoinette. That's the feeling I got from your
suggesting that I "make my own lunchbox", anyway."
messages.1413:
"But if you can't make one yourself, what about the rest of
your family?"
messages.1462:
"I don't particularly want to torture my stomach and
tongue."
messages.1539: "...No one's a good cook in your family?"
messages.1576:
"Even soldiers on the front lines, dying of starvation,
wouldn't eat what they would make."
messages.1674:
"But didn't you say as long as they made it for you, you'd
be happy... *cough cough*"
messages.1777:
I decided not to comment on the first half of what she said,
and fortunately the second half gave me the perfect chance.
messages.1940: "Uuuhn, I dunno. I haven't been feeling that well lately."
messages.1998:
"It must be the change of seasons. Shouldn't you take some
cold medicine? And get plenty of rest at night, as well."
messages.2107: "It's esssential to nip these things in the bud if you can."
messages.2239:
"You're just being so serious... I haven't seen you this way
very often."
messages.2317: "Well, it's good once in a while."

I gave a slightly disatisfactory smile, and bit into my
bread. It was Kotori's turn to stare at my face with a
serious expression.
messages.2463: I try and joke about it to relieve my discomfort a little.
messages.2623:
Her sudden words surprised the hell out of me. "onii-chan"
now?
messages.3001:
With the conversation coming to a standstill, I go back to
my bread.
messages.3105:
"In any case, thanks for your concern. I'd buy some cold

"Well, it'd be okay. I'm not too affected by colds or

Kotori appeared to be down with the cold, worrying me a fair

messages.141:
Taking a look behind the gym, I found a curious sight;
Tsukishiro exerting herself with all her heart.
messages.248:
Tsukishiro was digging all around the plant, then scooping
something inside the holes.
messages.387:
One of her dirtied hands motioned to the opened vinyl bag
next to her.
messages.457:
"Aha... so, protecting your precious plant from the evilness
of insects, and stimulating it's growth!"
messages.576:
She nodded, while continuing to mix the manure with the soil
around.
messages.636: Looknin at that plant, it does seem to be growing weaker...
messages.727:
Tsukishiro nodded again, this time slower than usual.
Slower, yet firmer and full of belief.
messages.815:
She really wants to make that plant bloom flowers... I
wonder why.
messages.907: "Hey, you're still not going to tell me why, huh?"
messages.952:
Tsukishiro turned to me, then gave me a little shake of the
head.
messages.1046:
My reason for coming here was to try and talk to Alice, but
in the end, I still can't seem to penetrate her A.T Field.
messages.1159: "Shall I get some water for the plant?"
messages.1211:
As usul for her thinking, her head tilted to the side,
until,
messages.1385:
Not being able to find anything appropriate around, I
eventually settled on a bucket at a deserted corner of the
school.
messages.1473:
I didn't want to make several trips back and forth, so I
filled it to the brim.
messages.1557:
She didn't say whether she wanted a lot or a little, after
all.
messages.1596:
With a bucket full of water in hand, I returned to the gym
rear.
messages.1742:
By the time I came back, she appeared to have finished
burying all the manure, and was just awating the water.
messages.1830: "With this much, it shouldn't be a...w, wahhh!"
messages.1989:
I stepped on a rock on the ground, losing my balance and
falling forward, emptying the bucket's contents in front of
me.
messages.2084:
The water fell onto the ground, of course, right around
Tsukshiro's plant. That had to be far more water than it
needed.
messages.2219: A puddle started to form, slowly soaking into the ground.
messages.2281:
Thanks to the digging up that Tsukishiro did, the area
around the plant was completely soaked.
messages.2455:
She simply shook her head, and started digging up more of
the soil, supplementing the soaked portion with it.
messages.2704:
Mimicking Alice, I started to do the same thing to the
drenched soil.
messages.2766:
With a lot of effort, the fertilizer and soil eventually
returned to what it was before my mishap.
messages.2842: I wiped my forehead, sighing in relief.
messages.2937:
"Uh, ahh... it was my fault. I'm sorry, I just got in the
way..."
messages.3001: Tsukishiro shook her head, this time fiercer than usual.
messages.3157: Repeating herself, she said a simple "Thank you" again.
messages.3223: "I'd come another time. Next time, I won't mess up."
messages.3539:
Attempting to help out Tsukishiro, I went to fetch some
water.
messages.3599:
But thanks to unsavoury events, I spilt it all onto the
ground.
messages.3675:
Instead of helping, I became a nuisance. What an idiot I
was...
messages.3737:
But Tsukishiro didn't criticize me. Instead, all she said
was "Thank you".
messages.3813: Perhaps she understood my good intentions...

"...We will meet again. As long as there is evil in the

Nemu's loud, evil laughter... was actually coming from a

messages.473: What kind of trickery are they up to now?
messages.518:
"No matter how many times you come back, we'd defeat you

messages.602:
Well, whatever. I continue to listen attentively to Nemu's
recital.
messages.656:
"(Good that someone else is reciting it. I wouldn't be able
to finish it myself, probably.)"
