messages.781:
"That no matter how many times the dragon king resurrected,
they, and their descendants, will always defeat it.
messages.1087:
There was a surprisingly good story hidden within the
textbook. Evil, dragon king, resurrection, justice--

messages.198:
She was walking around the shopping district randomly. Her
movements were like that of a pigeon.
messages.256:
That is, how a pigeon takes a few steps while constantly
turning it's head sideways, looking left and right
constantly.
messages.332:
Well, she probably needs something that requires her to pay
attention to everything in sight...
messages.498:
"Good afternoon. You should look in front of you when you
walk, you know?"
messages.599:
As I talked to Kotori, I noticed she was definitely
different from normal; she had a weird tension around her.
messages.696:
"If you could help me with something, everything should be
fine..."
messages.758:
"I'd be happy to fulfil your expectations. What's up? Are
you looking for someone?"
messages.846: I look around at the passers-by.
messages.939: As she said that, she waved behind me.
messages.1008: "Ah, here you are. I was looking for you, Kotori."
messages.1092:
Kudou waved back, with a smile showing his pearly-white
teeth. Ever-pleasant as usual.
messages.1212: I look back and forth at Kudou and Kotori.
messages.1350: "N, no! It's not what you think!"
messages.1408: Kotori had a rare bout of disconcertedness.
messages.1559:
Trying her hardest to convince me, she gave a big nod to my
question.
messages.1645: "Uhm, the truth is, I'm seatching for something..."
messages.1716: "We met by chance while walking here, so I decided to help."
messages.1782:
I met Kotori by chance, and Kotori met Kudou by chance.
Nothing strange about that.
messages.1881: Meeting my chance happens all the time after all... hah.
messages.1946: "Recently, Kotori has been asking my help for everything."
messages.2002: Kudou grinned jokingly at Kotori with his words.
messages.2039:
I wonder what kind of things Kotori has been asking his help
for to make him smile like that... well, whatever.
messages.2157: "Well, of course. Two heads are better than one."
messages.2217:
"So, with these human-wave tactics at hand, what exactly are
we looking for?
messages.2352:
"Ahh, I see... Koyomi-sensei's about to hit the big 6-0,
huh..."
messages.2440:
"Eh? Really? I've always thought she looked a bit
younger..."
messages.2606:
"Geez, if she had heard it, she'd be crushing both of you
like insects now."
messages.2756: Kotori put her finger to her lips teasingly.
messages.2842: We definitely can't get anything weird for her though."
messages.2939:
"My sister's tired of weird presents, since she doesn't
really have any special interests that have good present
ideas."
messages.3030:
"And she's recently learned the Hakkyokuken fighting
style..."
messages.3136:
"Is that so... we better be careful about what we get for
her, then..."
messages.3204:
Kudou murmured, obviously not experienced in matters
involving Koyomi-sensei.
messages.3407: Kotori unconciously glaced at Kudou's face.
messages.3505:
"With that kind of face, anyone could forgive him. He could
act like an uncaring idiot to girls and no one would punish
him!"
messages.3704: "Well, if you want to believe that, please do so."
messages.3753: "Unfortunately, I don't have much choice but to."
messages.3798:
I have to work hard for the natural advantages that a pretty
face gives... such a pitiful matter.
messages.3878:
Well, I suppose "working hard" for that isn't that much of a
chore either.
messages.3954:
"Well, if it's not the big 6-0, then what's the present for?
A normal birthday one?"
messages.4036:
It's nowhere close to Christmas, so that's the only reason I
could think of.
messages.4100:
Kudou also looked towards Kotori with interest. Neither of
us had heard the actual reason for the present, apparently.
messages.4315: "Mmm, not quite. It's for her ma--"
messages.4375:
She cut herself off mid-speech, her eyes round and her hand
on her mouth.
messages.4439: "Ma..? Her mother? And yours too, I guess?"
messages.4620:
Her face showed regret about what she almost said, as she
shook her head furiously.
messages.4671: "Well, if you can't say it, it's okay."
messages.4750: "I'm sorry. Just treat it like a normal present."
messages.4810: Well, if that's how it is, I better not pry any further.
messages.4896: "So anyway, could you go with me to choose a present?"
messages.5014: "Didn't I say so earlier? Three heads are better than two."
messages.5076: "...That's a bit different from earlier, I think."
messages.5151: Kotori gave me the thumbs up.
messages.5192: Somehow, I got an uneasy feeling from this...
messages.5555:
For apparently unspeakable reasons, I met Kotori while she
was searching for a present for Koyomi-sensei.
messages.5625:
We hooked up with Kudou on the way, and she asked whether I
could search together with her...

messages.294: A quizzical noise emitted from both of their throats.
messages.335:
"Leave it to me! I know what kind of presents
Koyomi-sensei's... womanly nature would want!"
messages.507:
"After all, you shouldn't get someone as... unique as
Koyomi-sensei a normal type of present, would you?"
messages.677: Kotori crossed her arms, her brow furrowing with thought.
messages.721:
"So what you're basically saying is, you don't think she'd
like any stereotypical gift?"
messages.857:
"I'm worried that you might go too far into the other end of
the spectrum..."
messages.962:
Suginami's more the type to ask what kind of present would
be appropriate, then buy the exact opposite. Far different
from me.
messages.1101:
With Kotori still pondering, Kudou laughed a little and
spoke up.
messages.1199:
"It'd be okay, I'd make sure he doesn't pick anything too
weird."
messages.1277:
"Weird? How rude. You'd have the fortune of seeing true
orginality at work!"
messages.1398: "That just worries me more, but... I'd trust you."
messages.1466: Kotori then started peering into my eyes.
messages.1526: "Although I wanted to go with you..."
messages.1645: "Well, good luck! I'd start searching over there."
messages.1703:
Leaving with a smile, Kotori disappeared within the crowd of
people.
messages.1784: Kudou was standing beside me. I patted his shoulder.
messages.1890: We left in the opposite direction.
messages.1964:
Although we looked around for ages, we weren't able to
decide on a present.
messages.2036: Everything I suggested was immediately rejected by Kudou.
messages.2083: I guess with all that I said, it was to be expected.
messages.2355: I went with Kudou to choose a present.
messages.2382:
Although I explained to Kotori my reasoning about what kind
of present was needed, she still had an uneasy look on her
face...
messages.2497: Well, in the end, we didn't decide anything anyway.

messages.461:
"But really don't choose anything like a joke for her,
okay?"
messages.538:
Half for her own feelings for her sister, and half because I
don't quite want to experience a Koyomi-sensei-style
crushing.
messages.680:
"Then, if you two are going to look over there... I'd stay
and look around here."
messages.754:
Kudou waved his hand at us, then disappeared into the crowd
of people.
messages.915:
"He's really popular, isn't he? It's like he knows all the
ways to get women to fall in love with him."
messages.1027:
"I don't think being popular has anything to do with that...
and I'm pretty sure he doesn't do that intentionally."
messages.1141: "I don't think he's one to lead people on intentionally."
messages.1186:
"That's pretty weird. How do you know so much about Kudou?
Are you two that close?"
messages.1298: "Not reaaaally... just call it women's intuition."
messages.1381:
"Then what does that women's intuition think about me? How
popular would I be around girls?"
messages.1551: You don't need to be that frank...
messages.1645:
Pointing an elegant finger forward, Kotori headed further
into the shopping district first, with her servant following
behind.
messages.1842:
In the end, despite how much we and Kudou looked around the
place... we still couldn't decide on a present.
messages.1949:
Well, she told us that whatever it is isn't that important
yet, so it'd be okay.
messages.2197:
I didn't know how helpful I'd be, but I went along with
Kotori anyway.
messages.2292:
--We all searched deep into the night, but walked away with
nothing.

messages.145: The shrine will do just fine.
messages.162:
Now that the noisy little things are gone, just the ambient
sounds of nature remained.
messages.226:
For someone who enjoys peace and quiet, it's no surprise
that I ended up here.
messages.349:
The refreshing breeze, and the sky that seemed so close... I
breathed it all in deeply.
messages.484: When, a voice called out to me.
messages.509:
I turned around to see the Miko-uniform-clad Tamaki, with
the Shime rope in her arms.
messages.638: "I was searching for a leisurely place, and ended up here."
messages.738: "That must be heavy... let me carry it."
messages.844: "Don't be so restrained. We're friends, right?"
messages.885: I firmly took the Shime rope from her shoulder.
messages.992: Smiling at her, I slung the rope around my shoulder.
messages.1059:
I felt like the entire area around me increased in gravity
by a factor of 2.
messages.1115: That was how heavy the rope felt.
messages.1146: A person can actually walk while carrying this...?
messages.1395:
"N, not quite... I came all this way carrying it, after
all."
messages.1496: Or maybe, the stubborn one was me.
messages.1600:
"You need this to be at the front shrine, right? ...Leave it
to me."
messages.1743:
As heavy as it was, Tamaki's bright face was all the
motivation I needed.
messages.1832: Well, spending days like this, isn't a bad thing.
messages.1984: After all that physical labour, my stomach was grumbling.
messages.2019: "I could go for some of the park's crepes right now."
messages.2152: "Don't tell me... you don't know about them."
messages.2229: "So you mean... you've never eaten one."
messages.2272: Tamaki shook her head from side to side.
messages.2305:
...Sensei, one of the seven wonders of the world is right
here.
messages.2346:
Someone who, at this place, in this day and age, has never
heard of the park's crepes...
messages.2406:
Tamaki must be really special, working in a place so far
seperated from the rest of the world...
messages.2484: "Well then, follow me. It's time for a lesson in society."
messages.2668:
As usual for the crepe store, there was a huge line of
mostly females queueing up.
messages.2742:
Eventually, we found a bench, me with my strawberry
chocolate crepe, and her with her blueberry cream crepe.
messages.2896: Tamaki peered at the crepe from side to side.
messages.2954:
It was the curious look someone would give to a foreign
delicacy.
messages.3003: ...I suppose, in practical terms, that is what a crepe is.
messages.3134: I watched her closely, waiting to observe her first bite.
messages.3181:
I wanted to see how someone who react to finally finding a
reason why life is wonderful.
messages.3674:
"Letting a little spill over, only makes the taste that much
better."
messages.3748:
Well, not really, but there's something about smearing a
little on your cheek, and exclaiming about it.
messages.3871: ---I kinda want to see how that'd look on her.
messages.3906:
My imagination was quickly crafting an image of Tamaki with
white cream smeared on her cheek.
messages.4050:
Tamaki gave the crepe one final glance, then steadfastedly
lowered her head.
messages.4185: Tamaki's face suddenly broke out in a smile.
messages.4229:
Not the usual elegant and refined smile, but one of pure
innocence and enjoyment, like a kid's smile.
messages.4313: It was a smile so infectious, it was making me smile too.
messages.4363: "Hmm... so normal females eat this sort of thing."
messages.4498:
"You think so? There are things everyone feels are
suspicious about me..."
messages.4576: "Well, in my eyes, you're simply a normal, cute girl."
messages.4719:
Although after a slight bout of nervousness, she quickly
returned to her usual, calm and collected self.
messages.4833: "My life really has changed today, thanks to Asakura-sama."
messages.4897: "I had a treat too, no need to thank me."
messages.4972:
"No... you helped me carry the rope, and introduced me to
crepes."
messages.5063: "Please teach me more things in the future."
messages.5104: "Of course, as long as you're willing to listen."
messages.5139:
With her getting so excited about the crepe, it certainly
made me want to introduce more new things to her.
messages.5226: We left the park together, in the direction of the shrine.
messages.5449: At the shrine, I saw Tamaki lugging a heavy object around.
messages.5515:
Seeing the sorry sight, I took it from her and carried it
myslf.
messages.5581:
As a thanks for my labour, she treated us to crepes at the
Sakura Park.
messages.5678:
It was the first time Tamaki had tried crepes, and she was
greatly moved by it.

After the evening's convenience store-bought dinner and a

I have to set my alarm clock, since Nemu's on disciplinary

I crept under the covers, and let the darkness overtake

The class was talking about the graduation party, but what

I rose from my bed, and covered my yawning mouth with my
hand.

breakfast. I got up from bed, changed into my uniform, and

Looking to the side of the school gates, Miharu was waving

While answering her, I grinned and placed my forehead on

I waved my hand behind me after I heard Miharu's voice, as I

On the way to school I saw Nemu and Miharu in front of the

Ignoring the surprised Nemu, I calmly counted while feeling

Returning to the physics classroom, a voice I didn't want to

"Ahh, if it isn't Shirakawa-sensei? You're looking even more

"Don't bother flattering me. I can tell that's not what

"Correct. It's a very... amazing score, you see? That's why

Koyomi-sensei, looking like the spitting image of a devil,

I was about to protest that it felt like I was getting
arrested, but then, she'd probably reply with "I AM the

"Oh really? Are you trying to say you were aiming to get 7
marks?"

"Don't try to fool me... if that was true, you'd have gone

"Manly, huh. Do you know what I think is manly? 100 marks.

"And I'd say that number is luckier than any I can think

messages.1740:
I was reeling from the verbal punches she was giving me,

messages.1952: Taking a closer look, it was,
messages.2156:
"Eh, ahh, that's right. I asked you to come when you were

Tsukishiro quietly entered the room, closing the door behind

messages.2315:
"This is about... I don't know whether it's my place to be

"Well, Tsukishiro, about that doll... I know it's very

"Yes, I know that. But school isn't the same as a

"W, well well. Tsukishiro, what she's trying to say, is to

"Alright, Tsukishiro, just be careful next time! And hurry

Glaring at me, Koyomi-sensei started fishing for a cigarette
in her pockets.
messages.3465:
"Tsukishiro, that's enough. You can go now. Just be careful

messages.3591:
Upon hearing Koyomi's words, she nodded respectfully, then
left as quietly as she came.
messages.3752: "Asakura, what do you think you were doing there?"
messages.3799:
At the sound of the door being shut tightly, the room was
instantly overcome with the mixed scent of oil and cigarette
smoke.
messages.3865:
"It's just that, you can't stop her from holding that
doll... it's very very important to her."

"I know that too. If it wasn't so important, she wouldn't be

messages.4076:
"Then, you didn't have to expressedly call her just to warn

"If I wasn't a teacher, I wouldn't mind either. I'm not that

2~3 clouds of smoke were puffed out from her mouth,

"Not much, Tsukishiro and I have just talked about that a

"Well then, what is her reason exactly for that? My extent

messages.4682:
"I see, I see. In that case, if anything happens to her,

With a wide grin on her face, Koyomi-sensei was looking at

messages.5000:
"Stop your whining. I've always been worried about that kid
since the day she enrolled into this school."
messages.5112:
"Everytime I see her, she's alone. She never seems to talk
to anyone."
messages.5197:
"I would try to do something, but I'm a teacher. There's are

messages.5279: "Well, in truth, she doesn't really tell me much either."
messages.5373:
"Recently, it seems that Amakase has been attempting to talk
to her, perhaps to make friends with her. That would be

messages.5480:
"Tsukishiro said... that the only friend she has, is that

messages.5561:
"From the rumours I've heard, doesn't that doll talk thanks

messages.5714:
"That girl definitely needs someone by her side right now.

messages.5863:
"Hah, there's no need to think so long and hard about it.
Even if you do, that girl won't say one thing about it
anyway."
messages.6051:
"There are things that you can do. Sooner or later, they

messages.6206: "Mmm. I don't think it's something you can force to happen."
messages.6272:
"Well, both ways... I'm not the kind of person who can just
leave someone like Tsukishiro alone either."
messages.6390:
"Haha, that'd be just fine. --Anyway, Asakura. Have you
eaten yet? If you haven't, how about lunch at the cafeteria?
My treat."
messages.6560:
"Yup, it's fine once in a while. After all, You're not a
typical student to me."
messages.6661: As she spoke, she winked at me.
messages.6730:
"And about the test scores... I can't change the 7 mark one,
but I'd make sure you do well on the others. Treat it as
service."
messages.6841:
With a noise undeserving of her age, she then lifted herself
off her chair, and stood up.
messages.6915: Make sure I do well on the others... eh?
messages.6960: Well, I'm getting treated anyway, so who cares.
messages.7189:
Koyomi-sensei was furious with me about the tests, but then
Tsukishiro interrupted us, apparently having been called up
before.
messages.7271:
Sensei wanted Tsukishiro to be more careful about where she
took the doll, despite it being important to her.
Koyomi-sensei was worried for her.
messages.7372:
When Tsukishiro left, Koyomi-sensei told me that since she
was a teacher, there were boundaries between the two of them
that were hard to surpass.
messages.7489:
So I was to be her pillar of strength, to support her when
she needs it.
messages.7575:
I was treated to lunch at the caferteria, due to my
acceptance of her request.

messages.196:
Holding the attendance records in her hand, Koyomi-sensei
entered the classroom.
messages.276: "(And the usual tiresome look as well...)"
messages.319:
If she just did things differently once in a while, she
could liven up this time of the day.
messages.395:
Like rappeling from the school building and coming in
through the window...
messages.494:
"(...If that happened, I bet the tardiness rate will drop
dramatically.)"
messages.582:
Koyomi-sensei wearing something fluffy would certainly cause
some commotion.
messages.644:
"(It'd be a complete distinction from her actual
character...)"
messages.712:
Vowing to myself never to reveal this to anyone, HR quickly
ended.
messages.917:
Koyomi-sensei's usual HR. It'd be more interesting if she
shook things up a little.
messages.983:
Like breaking the window to enter the class, cosplay, or
wearing a fluffy costume.

messages.129:
In the noisy classroom, I kicked back into my chair and read
a magazine.
messages.197: The class was a stark contrast from the rest of the school.
messages.248:
"(When Wakui declares a self-study lesson, everyone
rejoices.)"
messages.295:
Wakui is more of a researcher than a teacher at heart, so
when the tests were over, both parties didn't want to
continue with lessons.
messages.390:
Nemu, actually doing self-study, took a look back at myself
reading a magazine, shook her head in disgust, and turned
her head back.
messages.503:
I stuck out my hand towards Kudou to borrow another
magazine.
messages.697:
With no exams to worry about, Wakui declared the class to be
a self-study one in order to further his own research. Kudou
and I exchanged magazines, and Nemu and I exchanged glares.

messages.152: Still in the classroom, I stretched as noon approached.
messages.189:
There's still lessons in the afternoon which won't be
self-studies, so I'd have to keep my energy up.
messages.453:
As lunch break approached, I stretched and thought of what
to do.

messages.178:
The air was tepid, as I looked up to the blue sky, the sun's
rays shooting into my eyes.
messages.246:
"Now that eating in the courtyard is no longer cold, that
means Feburary is definitely over..."
messages.353:
Then again, there's no real reason not to eat here even when
it is cold...
messages.443:
"Maybe coldness would prevent me from keeping my mind on
pondering my existence in this shallow world?"
messages.519: I muttered to myself as I took a bite out of my bread.
messages.571: A male student sat on the bench I was sitting on.
messages.744: I continue chewing on my bread.
messages.776:
"......You sure you don't want to know? It's rather
interesting, methinks."
messages.875: "If you want to tell me, then start from the beginning."
messages.1097: Kudou chipped in, sitting next to Suginami.
messages.1263:
Ignoring the head-holding Suginami, I question Kudou
further.
messages.1422:
"I heard from her classmates that she left early because of
a headache, and that it's a relatively common occurence for
her."
messages.1537: "Hmm... but why tell that to me?"
messages.1593:
"I thought you might want to know. You're her friend after
all."
messages.1720:
Now that I looked at it, Kudou's face did have more than a
touch of concern on it.
messages.1829:
I remove my gaze from Kudou and looked around the courtyard
absent-mindedly.
messages.1883:
Even while she's having a headache, I bet Kotori would still
be giving everyone around her a ready smile.
messages.1955:
That no matter her condition, she wants to show everyone
that she's fine and well.
messages.2027: It's for things like that that she's become the school idol.
messages.2095:
An idol, one who, no matter the situation, always keeps on
smiling.
messages.2196: "It can at least be deduced from the talk around."
messages.2340: "Well, there's a lot of people like that.
messages.2396:
There's one in my family as well who often gets sick, after
all.
messages.2445:
No matter what we say about how these people shouldn't
extend themselves, it's them who have to bear the weight of
their problems...
messages.2560: I thought this as I hunched over slightly.
messages.2593: Bit by bit, I continued consuming my bread.
messages.2626: Kotori... hope you feel better tomorrow.
messages.2682: That thought unconciously entered my head.
messages.2891:
In the courtyard, Suginami and Kudou dropped by to tell me
that Kotori had left school early today.
messages.2965: Kotori... hope you feel better tomorrow.

messages.145: The boxed lunch that Tamaki made, laid in front of me.
messages.182: I've never seen such a beautiful lunchbox before.
messages.221:
It wouldn't look out of place at the front of a gourmet
restaurant. It's the saviour of my afternoon.
messages.338:
This all started when I heard Tamaki's voice calling out to
me while heading out the classroom...
messages.514: "Does it look like I'm going lawn-mowing?"
messages.671:
Whoops, this isn't the time for idle conversation like
this...
messages.718:
If I don't get a move on, there won't be anything edible
left.
messages.769: "Sorry, Tamaki, but I have to hurry..."
messages.810: I started heading off to make my purchases, but...
messages.908: Her red face staring at the ground, she meekly addressed me.
messages.998: "A, are you perhaps, going to buy your lunch?"
messages.1171:
I could understand what she was saying, but not what she was
hiding.
messages.1277:
"Um, if it's no trouble to you... I made a little too much
for my own lunch... so I thought we could share it..."
messages.1431: "I, if it's a bother, it's fine..."
messages.1472:
"You made a little too much... you mean, you made it
yourself? Is it really okay for me to eat it too?"
messages.1579:
Her face, still boring holes into the floor, grew even
redder.
messages.1682:
Or maybe she thinks eating from the same box would be
embarassing?
messages.1723:
Although, if that was true, she wouldn't have asked me in
the first place...
messages.1785: Well, whatever. No point sweating the small stuff.
messages.1828:
My meal for today is decided, lucky for me. And Tamaki made
it, so it'd be fit for a king most likely.
messages.1998: "Er, it should be me thanking you, no?"
messages.2046: "No... from the bottom of my heart, thank you."
messages.2163:
Our goal was to find a deserted area. We eventually landed
at the gym rear.
messages.2327:
The sight before me taught me the real feeling of being
speechless.
messages.2407: Is today the first day of the new year?
messages.2434:
The lunchbox she made was a tray of, essentially, a
five-course meal.
messages.2492:
It was made entirely of typical Japanese food, all arranged
neatly and appetizingly.
messages.2672: The entire thing even came with plates.
messages.2717: This feels great, more like a picnic than a school lunch.
messages.2754: Seems like she's not girly only in looks.
messages.2842: "I do not know how good it tastes, but..."
messages.2889: My answer was simply to take the top of the stack of plates.
messages.3003: Tamaki was staring at me, slightly worried.
messages.3042:
I started with piece of stewed potato, and brought it to my
mouth...
messages.3127:
The harmony between the soy sauce and the sweetness of the
potato...
messages.3187: I exclaimed what I felt, without thinking about it.
messages.3218:
This is as far from Nemu's cooking as it gets. This is the
real thing.
messages.3274: Tamaki then breathed a sigh of relief.
messages.3331: "I'm glad... I worked hard on it."
messages.3441: What does she mean by that...?
messages.3478:
Before I came up with an answer, we'd finished the entire 5
courses.
messages.3561: I sipped from a can of tea, washing down that amazing meal.
messages.3700: The happiness in her voice was clear.
messages.3746: This really was way too much for one person to finish...
messages.3835: Maybe she made that much on purpose?
messages.3880:
My thoughts must've been clear on my face, as Tamaki then
began talking.
messages.4046: I'm probably giving myself too much credit.
messages.4075:
Asking whether she made it for me, would also be plain
embarassing, especially if I'm wrong...
messages.4137:
I'll just accept the goodwill, and leave any hidden
intentions untouched.
messages.4297: "If I make too much again, would you help me with it?"
messages.4357: "Isn't that different from how much you usually make?"
messages.4560: She's planning to overdo it again, isn't she...
messages.4604: I get to eat more tasty lunches after all.
messages.4635: That can only be a good thing.
messages.4836: On the way to buy my lunch, I bumped into Tamaki.
messages.4875:
Tamaki had made too much for her lunch, and wanted to share
it with me.
messages.4947:
After seeing and tasting the 5-course lunch for myself, I
definitely agreed that she had made too much.
messages.5013: Though maybe, she made that much on purpose...

messages.141:
Once school lets out tomorrow, there'd be no more reason to
go back.
messages.197:
Of course, it's not like I CAN'T, but there just wouldn't be
a reason for me to do so.
messages.259: However, there's still Tsukishiro's plant to think about.
messages.308:
When I'd think about it, I'd probably end up dropping by.
It's not a problem of distance, since the school is quite
close to my home.
messages.384:
And seeing those eyes of Tsukishiro, working so hard to make
that plant grow, protecting it, makes me feel that I can't
leave her alone.
messages.509:
Not to mention, comparing how it looked when I first saw it
to now, it seems ot have grown ever-so-slightly stronger.
messages.589:
"Tsukishiro, will it be all right if I stop by here every
now and then?"
messages.723:
Her reply was mumbled, her eyebrows knitted. Eventually, she
took off her gloves, and started caressing that doll...
Piros.
messages.860:
"As long as you promise not to do anything rash with the
plant, come whenever you want."
messages.936:
Unlike the tight-lipped Tsukishiro, the doll named Piros
seemed to love the sound of it's own voice.
messages.998:
"Of course I wouldn't. There's no reason for me to come here
just to do that."
messages.1118:
"Then that'd be fine, but... why would you want to come
here, Asakura-senpai?"
messages.1188:
"Well... I can't explain it very well myself, but I just
don't want to leave Tsukishiro alone."
messages.1406: "...You don't want to leave me alone?"
messages.1457: "...Yeah, I won't leave you alone too."
messages.1553: It's still immensely odd to converse wtih a doll.
messages.1586:
But maybe, it would be the same thing as talking to
Tsukishiro through it.
messages.1668:
In other words, maybe she has a power to make dolls
communicate her feelings for her.
messages.1740:
Tsukishiro may not like, or want to talk, but at times where
she does need to say something, using a doll to
communicate...
messages.1855: It's a strange theory, to be sure.
messages.1880: ...But I can't think of any other explanation.
messages.1927:
Having lived with fairlytale-like powers myself for so long
anyway, I'd hardly be able to pass phenomena like that off
easily.
messages.2048:
"Anyway, I'd drop by every now and then, if both of you
don't mind."
messages.2170: "Okay. I don't mind at all if you come for a visit."
messages.2310:
I aimed my question not at the doll, but at Tsukishiro. I
still wanted to hear it from the person herself.
messages.2608: "You can let me handle all the talking if you need me to..."
messages.2683: "...I also won't mind if senpai comes."
messages.2739:
Quickly after saying that, she took out the gloves from her
pocket.
messages.2883:
Putting on her gloves, grabbing her bag, and taking the
now-silent doll with her, she ran off towards the direction
of the park.
messages.3031:
It was a strange conversation, but it was the first time I
managed to get such an honest, upfront reply out of her.
messages.3126: Maybe, just maybe, her heart is starting to open up.
messages.3366: After tomorrow, I don't need to go to school anymore.
messages.3422:
So in turn, I asked Tsukishiro whether I could come by every
now and then, to check on the plant and them.
messages.3500:
Tsukishiro used the doll to answer "It's fine if you come".
Following up with "Why do you want to come?"
messages.3613:
I answered that I didn't want to leave her, or the plant,
alone. In turn, I asked whether she minded me.
messages.3734:
Although she stumbled and stuttered, she eventually manage
to answer, with her own voice, "I don't mind."
messages.3810: Maybe, just maybe, her heart is starting to open up.

messages.145:
Nemu, Suginami and I, as well as 6 other people, surrounded
the Hyakunin Isshu* playing cards.
messages.242: "Looks like the time has come for us to settle this."
messages.351:
"The one who gets first place shall be treated by everyone
else to a packet of juice."
messages.421: "First place... then what about last place?"
messages.493:
That bastard... he's already decided in his head who would
be first and who would be last.
messages.819: "Look alive you two, we're going to start."
messages.869:
Mako was standing at the front of the class, holding a piece
of paper.
messages.914: "(Nemu'd be our best shot at winning this...)"
messages.955:
The two of them are proven masters at this, no one would bet
otherwise. There's almost no point in anyone else even
trying.
messages.1153:
"---Sheltering the harvest-hut Of the autumn rice-field; And
my sleeves are growing wet With the moisture dripping."
messages.1221:
My eyes departed to the center of the circle we formed, and
I saw a hand passing through the stack of cards.
messages.1297: The owner of that hand was...
messages.1455:
"--Treading through the crimson leaves, The wandering stag
calls. When I hear the lonely cry, Sad--how sad!--the autumn
is."
messages.1608: "I won't lose to you so easily."
messages.1779:
"--The wide-stretched plain of heaven, Is the moon the same
That rose on Mount Mikasa In the land of Kasuga?"
messages.1847: I could hear someone picking up one of the cards.
messages.2008:
Nemu had a smile on her face, holding one of the playing
cards.
messages.2136: That was-- a speed too fast for the human eye--
messages.2262:
"--That I walk the fields in spring, Gathering green herbs,
While my garment's hanging sleeves Are speckled with snow."
messages.2511: I played Hyakunin Isshu with Suginami and Nemu.

messages.162: A well-dressed man was leaning on a tree at Sakura Avenue.
messages.222:
"Expecting something? ...But what would someone in a
business suit want with a school...?"
messages.339:
My curiosity piqued, I took shelter under a nearby tree as
well and waited.
messages.476:
After awhile, a person went up to meet the suited man. It
was Koyomi-sensei.
messages.630:
I couldn't hear them from here, but I could tell from their
expressions that Koyomi was angry for some reason.
messages.698: Shen then dragged the man out of the school campus.
messages.778:
"...I see. She probably didn't want the rest of the school
to see him."
messages.850:
"But what do those two have to do with each other? Maybe
they really are lovers..."
messages.918: It made me wonder for a bit.
messages.949: Shaking my head a few times, I continued down Sakura Avenue.
messages.1176:
After school, standing under a sakura tree, was a man in a
business suit, looking very out of place.
messages.1234:
Just who was that? As I was thinking, Koyomi-sensei
appeared.
messages.1298:
Maybe it's Koyomi-sensei's boyfriend!? If that's the case,
she definitely wouldn't want anybody in school to see him.

messages.188:
Across the park, I saw someone who looked like Kotori riding
on a Mamachari.
messages.287:
I gave her a big wave, partly to let her know that she was
on a collision course with me. She slowed her speed, braking
at my front.
messages.528:
"Your face is red, and your eyes are watery... were you just
overcome by your love for me?"
messages.669: Kotori giggled, tilting her neck to the side.
messages.718:
"It would happen to anyone who would view such a gallant
figure."
messages.804: "The big wave I gave you just now, you know."
messages.843:
I gave her a repeat performance of my chivalirious
behaviour.
messages.922: "...I don't see quite see the gallantry in that."
messages.1076:
"Maybe I'd try doing it in another direction... uhm, so what
happened?"
messages.1140:
I was getting embarassed with my overdone motions, so I
decided to stop the jokes.
messages.1248: She stuck her brilliantly red tongue out cheekily.
messages.1297: "A cold, huh... then right now, you're..."
messages.1366:
"Yes, I went to buy medicine from the pharmacy. Going
through the park is a shortcut to my home."
messages.1452:
She playfully rang her Mamachari's bell a few times, looking
a bit like a child.
messages.1520:
"I see. So that's why you're kicking around on that
Mamachari like a kid."
messages.1686:
"Anyway, I better be going now. I shouldn't stay outside too
long."
messages.1860:
She stopped pedaling for a second, and turned her head back
towards me.
messages.1939:
"You should be careful as well, I hope I didn't spread any
of my germs from talking to you..."
messages.2026:
After she said that, she turned back and continued pedaling,
her figure getting smaller by the second.
messages.2121:
I raised my voice. I wonder if she heard me... her pace
didn't change one bit, though.
messages.2238: I slowly make my way out of the Sakura Park.
messages.2321: And she said she was worried that I would catch it?
messages.2368:
"It would be better if her germs left her for me instead...
heh."
messages.2430:
I sent that joke along with my other thought to the distant
Kotori... get better soon.
messages.2516:
As I muttered that wish, it disappered into the flow of the
red-dyed sunset.
messages.2815:
I met Kotori while she was buying medicine from the
pharmarcy. She doesn't really look like she's suffering too
badly though...

messages.141:
With nothing to do, and not wanting to go home just yet, I
ended up at the shrine.
messages.207:
Originally, this was hardly a place I'd spend just killing
time.
messages.254:
But now that Tamaki is there... it's fun just talking with
her.
messages.295: She was there, sweeping as usual, under the archway.
messages.374: I called out to Tamaki, who was sweeping the floor calmly.
messages.474:
Tamaki leaned her hands on her broom, and smiled gently to
me.
messages.688: Tamaki's sudden change of topic was odd.
messages.717:
Why would my coming out of boredom be something happy for
her?
messages.809:
"Well, there are few people who would come to a shrine when
they have no purpose in mind."
messages.917: "Since you have such interest in it though, I'm happy."
messages.1005: "Well, it's any Japanese's tradition to visit shrines..."
messages.1061:
"....And, being able to talk to Asakura-sama... is always
fun for me."
messages.1244:
"My, is there something wrong? Bringing that up so
suddenly..."
messages.1279:
Tamaki brought her hand to her mouth, covering her slight
laughter.
messages.1348: "You seem to be a touch odd today, Asakura-sama."
messages.1441:
And I came here out of boredom in the first place... now
that I'm here, I didn't really know what to do.
messages.1521: I wonder what IS there to do in a place like this, anyway...
messages.1645: Is there anything to do here?
messages.1684: A prayer would take maybe 5 minutes, maximum.
messages.1744:
If I had to choose, I'd rather just stay here and talk more
with Tamaki.
messages.1810:
"--Ah yeah, why don't you lend me your broom? Since I'm
here, I might as well help clean up the place."
messages.1953:
"Yeah, it'd be tough to clean this whole big place alone.
And we can talk while sweeping, anyway."
messages.2080: "Okay then! Please use this, I will retrieve a new broom."
messages.2153: She disappeared inside the shrine shortly after.
messages.2205:
I awaited her reappearance, as the wind scattered her
gathered leaves.
messages.2271: She eventually returned with another bamboo-stick broom.
messages.2379:
We started sweeping all the nearby leaves into a single
pile.
messages.2420: Mixed among the pile of leaves, was a cigarette butt.
messages.2496: "Geez, these people who treat a shrine as a rubbish bin..."
messages.2573:
"There are many worshippers who aren't as upstanding as you,
I'm glad you're here to help..."
messages.2643:
"Oh yeah, it used to be that the shrine wouldn't allow
people to take rocks back with them, right?"
messages.2751:
"That used to be true, but now, children do it all the
time."
messages.2841:
"We'd draw on an empty sidewalk, and used to play
hopskotch..."
messages.3041: "If you mean memories of my childhood, sure I do, but..."
messages.3113: I tilted my head in thought.
messages.3138:
Now that Tamaki said it, i don't really have anything
memorable of this shrine.
messages.3326: Tamaki seemed to sigh a little.
messages.3359:
"Are you referring to that "deep bond" that we're supposed
to have?"
messages.3476:
She was staring at the floor again, thinking hard about
something.
messages.3637: "Well... I really don't have any memories of that either."
messages.3703:
I don't remember anything, but doubtlessly, if there was
something, it would be during my childhood days.
messages.3779:
But to have both of us unable to remember it... makes me
curious.
messages.3863: Just what is that bond that connects the two of us?
messages.3910: In the middle of my train of thought,
messages.3973:
"This is a marvelous sight... shall we rest for a little
while?"
messages.4129:
Stopping our sweeping, we set our gathered leaves ablaze in

messages.4226: "Hehe, it's a little out of the season for this, but..."
messages.4263:
Tamaki was roasting a mochi over the fire, wherever she

messages.4409:
"Nah, it'd be good because of what it is, not what it's
not."
messages.4457: The mochi swelled slowly from the roasting.
messages.4521:
We sat around the campfire, blowing air at our heated mochis
to cool them down.
messages.4583: Just what is that deep bond...
messages.4798:
With time on my hands, I ended up at the shrine, helping
Tamaki to sweep up the surroundings.
messages.4847:
Tamaki, trying to find out the deep bond between us, tried
to dig out my childhood memories...
messages.4913: But unfortunately, I just couldn't remember anything.
messages.4989:
In the end, we just sat around a bonfire, eating roasted
mochis.

messages.148:
I sat on my bed, looking at the calendar hanging on the
wall.
messages.202: Tomorrow is when classes end for the semester.
messages.235:
From the time the graduation party preparations begin to
when I enter my new school, leaves me about one month of
rest.
messages.327:
"There will still be school after tomorrow, but attendance

messages.385: Wonder what I'd do for the last day of school...
messages.455:
In any case, as long as I don't get called to school for

going.

I took the alarm clock from my bedside table, and started

messages.730: After setting the alarm, I continued studying.

I lay my head on the pillow, and stared into the ceiling.
--A smile slowly lit up my face.
messages.262: The last day of school is always fun.
messages.327: I feel my eyelids getting heavier, and slowly close my eyes.
messages.420: T'is the best way of falling asleep.
messages.666:
The last day of school is always a fun time. After setting
the alarm clock, I slowly fall asleep grinning, with that
thought in mind.

"This ends the classes for this semester. Those with

messages.419:
From here on, it's as good as vacation. Tomorrow, attendance
won't be taken in the morning anymore, and I'm not joining
events.
messages.538: "(Well, even so, it'd have nothing to do with me.)"
messages.579: Now then... what should I do.
messages.763:
It's finally over, all the classes. Tomorrow attendance
won't be taken, and I have nothing to do regarding the
graduation party, so there's no reason for me to be here
again.
messages.896: Now then, what should I do.

messages.237: "Whatever are you talking about? It's not the final day."
messages.286: "Don't look at me with those eyes..."
messages.342:
"The graduation party is on the 15th. There's still one week
to go."
messages.406:
"But for the third years, this IS the last day of school.
Aren't you sore that the disciplinary committee makes you
come back?"

messages.697:
"My job, to prevent the the roots of evil, like you and
